courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Placement in a medical office for a guided experience providing the student with a practical application of learned medical office administrative skills. Direct supervision will be the responsibility of a designated person at the site. The students will spend 20 hours per week for 10 weeks, for a total of 200 hours in assigned clinical rotations.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Introduction to Health Professions
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Offered at Missoula College. Students learn about the various healthcare degrees and career pathways through guest speaker presentations, discussions, and writing assignments.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.desc: Offered every term. Introduction to a medical word building system using Greek and Latin word roots, combining forms, suffixes, and prefixes.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Medical Billing Fundamentals
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Prereq. or coreq., AHMS 220. An introduction to insurance claim processing for the major medical insurance programs. Students will be provided with a basic knowledge of CPT and ICD-10 procedural and diagnostic coding. Emphasis on completing universal insurance forms to maximize reimbursement as well as troubleshoot denied or underpaid claims.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Beginning Procedural Coding
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., AHMS 156 and BIOH 112. Foundation for utilizing the CPT coding system to increase compatibility and comparability of medical data among users and providers.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: AHMS 164 Beginning Diagnosis Coding: ICD-10
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., AHMS 156 and BIOH 112. This course covers basic and intermediate levels of theory and application of ICD-CM principles and guidelines for coding and sequencing diagnoses and procedures. Students perform basic and intermediate coding using real health records, case studies, and scenarios. Application will focus on the use of the electronic ICD-10-CM with an overview of encoder software. This coding class involves hands-on coding, and knowledge of basic use of applicable coding books or the electronic ICD-10-CM. Currently the students take this course through Great Falls

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: CPT Coding
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Students must have completed AHMS 160 and AHMS 201 through Great Falls-MSU prior to taking this course. Comprehensive application of the CPT coding system to assign codes for services, supplies and equipment for comparative analysis, research and reimbursement.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: ICD-10 CODING
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., AHMS 164 and AHMS 201 (taken at Great Falls-MSU). Basic understanding of diagnostic and procedural coding principles should already be established. The course requires interpreting ICD-10-CM coding and reporting guidelines to sequence and assign appropriate diagnostic codes for both inpatient and various outpatient settings. Compliance issues associated with various IPPS reimbursement systems such as MS-DRGs, as well as APCs are covered. Encoder software will complement the ICD-10-CM manual in the application of coding processes. Clinical information will be interpreted from brief case studies and progress to the coding of health record excerpts.
courses.prereq: AHMS 164 and AHMS 201 (taken at Great Falls-MSU)

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Products
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Fundamental principles of pharmacology and the implications of medication use. Includes the law as it pertains to drug use, dosage forms, routes of administration as well as the pharmacologic actions and uses of drugs.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Medical Office Procedures
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. An introduction to the necessary skills and qualities required to function successfully in the medical arena. Emphasis on medico-legal and ethical responsibilities, records management and financial management of the medical practice, and interpersonal communications to include patient reception, telephone techniques and appointment scheduling.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Computerized Medical Billing
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., or corequisite AHMS 156 and AHMS 220. A medical package is used to enter and update patient data, enter charges, payments and adjustments, and generate management reports, insurance forms, and patient statements.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Medical Ethics
courses.desc: Offered every term. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to Missoula College Pre-Health and Health Professions majors and Mountain Campus Pre-Pharmacy and Pre-Nursing students. Ethical decision-making tools for addressing common ethical issues in the health professions.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Friday Morning Medical Conference
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered fall and spring semesters. Offered at Missoula College. Students attending will learn about a variety of concepts, medical approaches, and health-care related issues impacting health care practitioners in a variety of settings. This course is a weekly webinar presentation (video-conferencing delivery method) with reflection to follow. The material presented each semester is different, so students can take the course more than once. CR/NCR grading only.

courses.subject: AHMS
courses.title: Medical Information Internship
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Students should be enrolled in final semester in the Medical Information Technology program and have a minimum grade of C in Allied Health Medical Support (AHMS) courses. On-the-job training in positions related to each student's career goal in the medical office field. This experience increases students' skills, prepares them for initial employment, and increases occupational awareness and professionalism. Students work a minimum of 135 hours at an approved site. Offered for CR/NCR grading only.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Patient Care in Radiology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. All program pre-requisites must be completed, and student must be accepted into the program. Introduction to the concepts and practices necessary to provide quality patient care in the diagnostic imaging department. Course covers legal and ethical standards of care, basic nursing practices, infection control, venipuncture, and etc, as well as medications and contrast agents used in radiology.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Imaging I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. All program prerequisites must be completed, and student must be accepted into the program. Introduction to physics of x-ray production. Includes introduction to field of diagnostic imaging and presents factors of image quality and exposure methods: density, contrast, recorded detail, distortion.Also includes introduction to digital imaging concepts.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Methods
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. All program prerequisites must be completed, and student must be accepted into the program. Course covers the knowledge and skills necessary for quality patient care during standard and specialty radiographic procedures, as well as an introduction to image evaluation.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiology Lab
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. All program pre-requisites must be completed, and student must be accepted into the program. Students will practice all patient positioning skills necessary for competency as Radiologic Technologists.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Methods II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Advanced and less common radiographic procedures are introduced including fluoroscopy, surgery and various other procedures.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Methods II Lab
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Students will practice patient positioning skills necessary for competency as Radiologic Technologists.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Clinical I
courses.desc: (R-20) Offered over three semesters throughout the Radiology Technology program, beginning autumn semester. Offered at Missoula College. Students will begin with an introduction to patient management and basic radiographic procedures. The final semester offers opportunities in advanced patient management skills and experience with highly skilled radiographic procedures. Each semester builds on the previous semester, always emphasizing the principles of ALARA.
courses.offered: over three semesters throughout the Radiology Technology program, beginning autumn semester

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Imaging II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Offers students more technical and detailed information on the use of image receptor systems, processing principles, and imaging modalities used in radiology.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiobiology and Radiation Protection
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Principles of radiation protection and radiobiology. Topics include the effects of ionizing radiation on body tissues, protective measures for limiting exposure to the patient and personnel, and radiation monitoring devices.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Registry Review
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. An overview of imaging concepts as a review for the national certification test. Topics include a systematic approach for image evaluation, patient care, radiation protection and the physics of radiographic imaging.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Cross Sectional Anatomy
courses.desc: Course offered online spring semester. Offered at Missoula College. Students must be program graduates or ARRT certified with a current state license to register for the CT courses. This course will cover sectional anatomy (axial, sagittal and coronal planes), contrast media (types, contraindications, administration), imaging processes (scout acquisition and methods, parameter selection, protocol modification), and special procedures (reformatting, 3-D rendering, biopsies/drains, screening).

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Physics and Instrumentation
courses.desc: Course offered online spring semester. Offered at Missoula College. Students must be program graduates or ARRT certified with a current state license to register for the CT courses. This course will cover information specific to ARRT guidelines in preparation for the Computed Tomography Exam. The course will be broken down in to the following sections: patient assessment and preparation, contrast administration, radiation safety, and dosimetry.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Radiographic Clinical II
courses.desc: (R-22) Offered over two semesters in the Radiology Technology program: summer semester for 12 credits and fall semester for 10 credits. Offered at Missoula College. Students will begin with an introduction to patient management and basic radiographic procedures. The final semester offers opportunities in advanced patient management skills and experience with highly skilled radiographic procedures. Each semester builds on the previous semester, always emphasizing the principles of ALARA.

courses.subject: AHXR
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. Extended classroom experience which provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Patient Care & Assessment
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., BIOH 201N. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Introduction to nursing- related knowledge and skills with emphasis on application of microbiology to aseptic technique. Assessment of the respiratory system with cardiopulmonary diagnostic and laboratory tests interpretation. Observation and interpretation of overall patient condition is integrated throughout the course.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Fundamentals I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Orientation to basic respiratory care science including the application of principles of physics and chemistry. Emphasis on theory, operation and troubleshooting of equipment used at the entry level of practice. Introduction to airway pharmacology. Principles of basic chemistry introduced with an application to pharmacology as related to the pulmonary system.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Fundamentals II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., AHRC 131. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Study of the indications, rationale, methods, instrumentation, and analysis of Blood Gases. Emphasis will be placed on the physiology and clinical implications of acid-base abnormalities. Cardiovascular and related pharmacology studied in preparation for ACLS and ventilator management. Microbiology in relation to equipment processing, pulmonary rehabilitation, respiratory care in alternative settings, patient education, and health promotion.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Lab I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Basic clinical competencies taught in AHRC 131 are studied in a laboratory setting. Peer and instructor review of competencies included. Students earn their BLS certification. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Pharmacology for Respiratory Diseases
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Missoula College Respiratory Care program. This course covers the concepts and principles of pharmacology required in the practice of respiratory care, including medications, actions, dosages, routes of administration, and adverse reactions. Topics include patient education of medication delivery devices, patient monitoring devices, utilization techniques, and the standards for therapeutic efficacy in relation to diseases and conditions of the cardiopulmonary system.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Critical Care
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Continuation of AHRC 131. Physiology, indication, contraindications, and application of mechanical ventilation. Emphasis on patient assessment, monitoring, stabilization and weaning during assisted pressure breathing. Analysis of the various modes of ventilation, including optimizing the patient-ventilator interface in the adult through various advanced airway techniques.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Pathology & Disease
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Special lectures in medicine and disease as related to the cardiopulmonary system. Emphasis on recognition of signs and symptoms of disease and implications for treatment through the study of selected case studies.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Anatomy & Physiology
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Principles of physiologic chemistry are introduced and applied to the macro and micro anatomy of the cardiopulmonary system with a focus on structure and function. Application made to pathology and assessment of patients receiving mechanical ventilation.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Perinatal & Pediatric Respiratory Care
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Study of perinatal and pediatric respiratory care with emphasis on assessment, resuscitation and mechanical ventilation of the neonate and pediatric patient. The theory of Neonatal Resuscitations (NRP) will be presented. Neonatal and pediatric diseases will be studied.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Lab II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. A continuation of AHRC 150 with emphasis on adult critical care. Clinical competencies taught in AHRC 231 and AHRC 235 are studied in a laboratory setting. Peer and instructor review of competencies included. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Review
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. A review of respiratory care in preparation for credentialing exams. Students must take an Entry Level Self-Assessment Exam, a Written Registry Self- Assessment Exam, and a Clinical Simulation Self-Assessment Exam.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Clinical Experience I
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program.Emphasis on the student directly performing basic clinical skills in a patient care setting to include hospitals, home care, and pulmonary function laboratories. Students also participate in physician rounds. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Lab III
courses.desc: Offered summer. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Students study principles and theory of advanced life support. Peer and instructor review are included. Students will be Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) and Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) certified at the end of this class. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Clinical Experience II
courses.desc: Offered summer. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Continuation of clinical skills learned in AHRC 255. Introduction to adult critical care along with sleep and cardiac diagnostics. Students also participate in physician rounds. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Respiratory Care Lab IV
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Emphasis on neonatal and pediatric critical care. Clinical competencies introduced in AHRC 243 are studied. Peer and instructor review of competencies are included. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Clinical Experience III
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Respiratory Care program. Emphasis on neonatal and pediatric critical care. Clinical competencies introduced in AHRC 243 are studied. Peer and instructor review of competencies are included. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: AHRC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Introduction to Surgical Technology
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Provides an orientation to the scrub and circulatory roles of the surgical technologist in the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative periods. Entry level skills and theories are emphasized.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Lab I
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Demonstration of sterile technique in the campus lab, various skills, and their application in the operating room. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Pharmacology
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., M 105 or 115 or M 121 or M 151 or M 171. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Basic overview of the medications commonly used before, during, and after a surgical procedure.
courses.prereq: M 105 or 115 or M 121 or M 151 or M 171

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Operating Room Techniques
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., AHST 101, AHST 115, and AHST 154. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Focus is on the scrub and circulator roles of the surgical technologist in the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative periods, more complex skills and theories, and the impact of new technologies in the 21st century operating room.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Procedures I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., AHST 101, AHST 115, and AHST 154. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. A study of surgical procedures following the patient through the preoperative, intraoperative, and post-operative stages of specific surgical specialties.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Procedures II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. A study of surgical procedures following the patient through the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative stages of specific surgical specialties.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Lab II
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Demonstration of more complex skills in the campus lab, including assistant circulating, and their applications in the operating room. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Clinical I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Perioperative experience in minor surgical procedures through a supervised clinical hospital rotation.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Clinical II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Perioperative experience in major surgical procedures through a supervised clinical hospital rotation.

courses.subject: AHST
courses.title: Surgical Internship
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Restricted to students in the Surgical Technology program. Capstone experience in the perioperative role in preparation for initial employment, increasing occupational awareness and professionalism. Students take call for emergency surgeries alongside experienced hospital staff.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Anthropology & the Human Experience
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Offered intermittently in summer. A survey of anthropology which introduces the fundamental concepts, methods and perspectives of the field. The description and analysis of human culture, its growth and change. The nature and functions of social institutions.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Ancient Migrations
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. An exploration of migrations in human prehistory and history as known from DNA studies, the archaeological record, historical linguistics, the human fossil record and history. How these migrations have impacted the culture, institutions, and biology of contemporary societies and populations.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Race and Minorities
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Analysis of the development and concept of race as a social category and the processes of cultural change within and between ethnic groups.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Food and Culture
courses.desc: Offered spring. Examination of the ways culture shapes the satisfaction of a biological need; food production, preparation, choices, customs, taste, taboos, beverages, spices and food distribution around the globe.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: The Silk Road
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to the study of the human communities, cultures, and economies in Central and Southwest Asia along the ancient four thousand mile-long Silk Road.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeology of Yellowstone: 11,000 Years of Native Americans in Yellowstone National Park
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Introduces students to the Native American prehistory and history of Yellowstone National Park, from 11,000 years ago to the present. The focus is on archaeological sites in the various areas of the park, including lakes, mountains, obsidian sources, rivers, and geyser basins.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Anthropology for Majors: Understanding the Four-Field Approach
courses.desc: Offered spring. This course is designed as an advanced low-level undergraduate overview of the four-field approach to the study of anthropology. Students will learn about each of the four fields of Anthropology, including Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, Cultural Anthropology, and Linguistics. While this course is introductory, it will employ innovative curriculum for students who are majoring in anthropology. Each semester, faculty will use one or more major anthropology research issues as a guiding matrix for the dissemination of anthropological concepts. The course is intended for low-level undergraduate students either majoring in anthropology or considering a major in the discipline. This course also provides career guidance for students considering job opportunities in the four sub-areas of Anthropology.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Anthropological Statistics
courses.desc: An introduction to the statistical methods and reasoning used by anthropologists. Course requires used of a Windows or Macintosh computer and will utilize free statistics software the student must run on their computer.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. An introduction to human evolutionary biology including processes of evolution, primate studies, hominin paleontology, and human variation.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Biological Anthropology Lab
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., or corequisite ANTY 210N. This lab course allows students to more deeply explore the concepts and materials covered in Introduction to Biological Anthropology. Students will engage in lab based activities involving human genetics and processes of evolution, biology and behavior of non-human primates, human evolution, and modern human adaptation and variation.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Culture & Society
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Study of social organization of non-western societies; emphasis on variations in ecology, social structure, economic, political and religious beliefs and practices.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Central Asian Culture and Civilization
courses.desc: Offered autumn even numbered years. Introduction to Central Asia's history, culture and ways of thinking. Focus on the political and social organization of Central Asia and cultural changes as expressed in art and interactions with China, India and the Middle East.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Intro to Archaeology
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. What archaeologists do and how they reconstruct past human cultures. Methodological and theoretical approaches to understanding and explaining past human societies.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeological Wonders of the World
courses.desc: Offered spring even numbered years. Prereq., WRIT 101 or WRIT 201. This course highlights the classical civilizations of the ancient world, fields such as Egyptology and Classical Archaeology, and the major archaeological discoveries which are associated with them.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings relating to current problems or new developments in the discipline.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Human Variation
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ANTY 210N. Introduction to human biological variation, and to the methods and theories that are used to explain the distribution of variable features.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Human Evolution
courses.desc: Offered autumn, odd-numbered years. Prereq., ANTY 210N. An exploration of the fossil and archaeological records of the evolution of human beings, and of current methods and theories used in interpreting these data.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Principles of Forensic Anthropology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ANTY 210N. A study of techniques for recovering skeletal material, identifying and interpreting human skeletal remains, keeping records, interacting with the law enforcement system and documenting human rights abuses.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Native Peoples of Montana
courses.desc: Offered spring. The history and culture of the Indian tribes in Montana.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Indigenous Peoples & the Ethics of Development
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. This class will examine the impact of global development on tribal and Indigenous peoples. Discussion topics will include ethical issues, land, health, employment, and cultural change caused by global development as well as explore how and why Indigenous societies resist or adapt to imposed changes.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Peoples and Cultures of World
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Study of the peoples of various geographic regions and their cultures.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Central Asia and Its Neighbors
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Analysis of the human communities and cultures of Central and Southwest Asia, with particular emphasis on the importance of relationships with neighboring countries and civilizations since ancient times.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeology of North America
courses.desc: Offered autumn. The origins, backgrounds and development of Pre-Columbian American peoples and cultures.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeology of Montana
courses.desc: Offered spring. The origins, distributions and development of aboriginal cultures in Montana and surrounding regions.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: PaleoIndian Archaeology
courses.desc: Offered spring or winter, even-numbered years. Examines archaeological, linguistic, biological and skeletal data to determine from where and when Native Americans arrived in North America. Examines archaeological sites from such diverse places as Montana, Siberia, Virginia, and Chile to answer the most intriguing question in contemporary American archaeology today: how, when and from where did people first arrive in the Americas?

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Mesoamerican Prehistory
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. The development of civilization and prehistoric states in the New World. Prehistoric lifeways and the effects of European contact on these cultures.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: History of Anthropology
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors and minors in Anthropology. The development of theory and method in cultural anthropology to the present. Various archaeological, ethnological and socio-psychological theories in the light of historical anthropology. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Anthropological Museology
courses.desc: Offered spring even-numbered years. Introduction to anthropological museums, museum work and museum theory. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Contemporary Issues of Indigenous Peoples
courses.desc: Offered autumn. An examination of the major issues that affect the contemporary experiences of Indigenous Peoples of the Americas, and other global communities. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Preceptorship in Anthropology
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., ANTY 210N or ANTY 220S or ANTY 250S. Assisting a faculty member by tutoring, grading objective exams, conducting review sessions, and carrying out other class-related responsibilities. Open to juniors, senior, and graduate students with consent of the faculty member with whom they serve. Proposals must be approved by department chair. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Osteology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ANTY 314. A detailed examination of the human skeleton with an emphasis on identifying individual bones and their structures. Specifically extended to fragmentary skeletal elements. Direct hands-on experience required. Level: Undergraduate/Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Forensic and Mortuary Archaeology
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., ANTY 314. Practical approaches to locating, documenting and recovering human skeletal remains, including surface scatters and burials. Emphasis on interpretations of evidence for recovery scene formation and mortuary behavior. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Forensic Anthropology and Bioarchaeology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ANTY 210N and either CJUS 125N or CJUS 488. An exploration of the principles, theories, and applications of forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology. The focus is on how information about a person’s identity and the lifeways of the society in which they lived is inferred from human remains in the criminal investigation context and the archaeological context. Level: undergraduate and graduate.
courses.prereq: ANTY 210N and either CJUS 125N or CJUS 488

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Emergence of Modern Humans
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., ANTY 210N. An exploration of the emergence of "modern" humans and their relationships with Neanderthals. Exploration of what it means to be "a modern human" through an examination of human evolutionary history. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Evolution and Genetic Variation in Human Populations
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq. ANTY 310. Human genetic variation examined from a molecular perspective. Emphasis on the role of infectious disease and other factors as a selective factor in human evolution and exploration of the implications of these associations for human genetic variation. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Mind, Culture, and Society
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. The study of socialization, personality, cognition, and mental health cross-culturally. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Social Anthropology
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., WRIT 101 or WRIT 201. Seminar style senior capstone course for cultural anthropology students. This course focuses on bringing theory and methods together in written and visual ethnography. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Ethnographic Field Methods
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., WRIT 101 or WRIT 201. Introduction to socio-cultural anthropological methods including participant observation, interviewing and narrative techniques and analysis of qualitative data. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Indigenous Global Health & Healing
courses.desc: The course examines traditional and contemporary uses of medicinal plants and spiritual healing within Indigenous North American societies. The class also examines the impact Indigenous people's knowledge of medicinal plants has had on non-Indigenous people's health as well as the field of medicine. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Cities and Landscapes of Central Asia
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Analysis of the main centers of civilization and culture, rich sites and monuments of Central Asia and Southwest Asia since ancient times. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Artistic Traditions of Central Asia
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Analysis of the study of human artistic creativity and scientific innovations of various cultures in Central and Southwest Asia since ancient times. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Cultural Resource Management
courses.desc: Offered autumn, odd-numbered years and intermittently in summer. Introduction to the laws and practice of cultural resource/heritage property management. Focus on the management of archaeological sites, historic structures, and traditional cultural places due to federal laws. Emphasis is on laying foundation of CRM practices for students interested in pursuing it as a potential career. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: GIS in Archaeology
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., ANTY 250S. Anthropological and archaeological data acquisition, management, and analysis using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) tools and techniques. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Lithic Technology
courses.desc: Offered autumn odd-numbered years. Analysis of stone artifacts and debitage. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Artifact Analysis
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., WRIT 101 or WRIT 201; and ANTY 250S. Laboratory approaches and techniques for analyzing material culture from technological, stylistic, and chronological perspectives. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Historical Archaeology
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., ANTY 250S. Understanding and interpreting the past through historical archaeological remains, methods, and theories. Focuses on historical archaeological sites and topics from the American West, but also examines the field’s global perspective. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeology of Hunter-Gatherers
courses.desc: Offered autumn even-numbered years. Introduction to the archaeological study of hunter-gatherer societies. Primary emphasis on archaeological method and theory. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeology of the Arctic and Subarctic
courses.desc: Introduction to the study of Arctic and Subarctic archaeology emphasizing the Pleistocene and Holocene prehistory of North America and eastern Siberia. Understanding of methodological problems associated with archaeology in a northern context, the evolution of Inuit, Eskimo, Aleut and Athapaskan cultures, and hunter-gatherer adaptations to northern interior and coastal environments. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeological Survey
courses.desc: (R-12) Prereq., ANTY 250S. Offered autumn. A field course in Montana archaeology. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeological Field School
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered summer and/or winter. Prereq., ANTY 250S. Provides students with a well-rounded experience in archaeological field methods. Field schools will typically occur at archaeological site locations away from campus. During the archaeological field experience, students may learn methods of excavation, survey, research, and analysis to facilitate their transition to careers as professional archaeologists. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Methods for Native Languages
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered spring. In an effort to highlight promising methodologies that will advance the success of Native language acquisition and instruction, students will be exposed to an innovative methodology while being instructed in an Indigenous language. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered every term. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Seminar/Workshop
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Field Experience/Practicum
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Organized field experience or language practicum in anthropology. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Practical application of classroom learning through internship in a number of areas such as museology, cultural resource management and forensics. Level: undergraduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Contemporary Anthropological Thought
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Anthropology. A review of major contributions to current anthropological theory, with an emphasis on the application of theory to anthropological problems. Significant advances in general theory, symbolic anthropology, critical theory, cultural studies, and postmodernism. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Applied Anthropological Statistics
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. Restricted to graduate students in Anthropology. A review of simple and multivariate, descriptive, and inferential statistical methods and their application to the students’ own thesis or dissertation data. Course requires use of a Windows or Macintosh computer and will use free software that students must run on their computers.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Seminar on Human Variation & Evolution
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn. Various topics related to genetic evidence of human biological evolution, morphological and genetic diversity of modern humans, and problems of "race". Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Advanced Forensic Anthropology
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered spring. Review of traditional methods and exploration of new methods of skeletal analysis, as applied to cases from the forensic collection. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Seminar in Bioarcheaology & Skeletal Biology
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered spring. Theoretical and methodological approaches to the analysis of human skeletal remains derived from archaeological contexts. Demography, health and disease, diet and nutrition, growth, activity patterns, and measures of biological relatedness are interpreted within a biocultural framework. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Theory & Methods in Bioanthropology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. A detailed review of the body of theory that is foundational for the study of human evolution, human variation, bioarchaeology, forensic anthropology, and primatology, along with a consideration of major methods used to analyze data in these fields. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Seminar in Contemporary Ethnography
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current ethnographic research. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Evolutionary Archaeology
courses.desc: Offered autumn even-numbered years. Examination of method and theory in Darwinian evolutionary archaeology. Seminar assignments and discussions focus on human behavioral ecology, cultural transmission, and macroevolution. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Archaeology and Collections Advanced Practicum
courses.desc: The course provides students with practical skills and experiences that will prepare them for working in dynamic and ever-changing fields such as anthropology, cultural heritage studies, heritage management and historic preservation, indigenous studies, museum studies, and public archaeology, with an emphasis on education, outreach, diplomacy, as well as creating culturally safe and respectful workspaces. The course’s internal coherence is grounded in preparing students for the complex ethical and legal challenges of heritage fields while also giving them an opportunity to contribute to UM’s institutional history of heritage collections management, which dates back to the university's 1893 founding and requires special attention since the 1990 enactment of NAGPRA. Co-convenes with ANTY 468. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Research
courses.desc: (R-10) Offered every term. Directed individual research and study appropriate to the background and objectives of the student. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-24) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered every term. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: Graduate

courses.title: Seminar/Workshop
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Field Experience/Practicum
courses.desc: (R-18) Offered intermittently. Organized field experience or practicum in anthropology. Level: Graduate.

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Anthropology. Practical application of classroom learning through internship in a number of areas such as museology, cultural resource management and forensics. Written reports are required. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Thesis/Professional Project
courses.desc: (R-10) Offered every term. Restricted to graduate students in Anthropology. Preparation of a thesis, manuscript, or professional project based on research for presentation and/or publication. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Issues in Cultural Heritage
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Doctoral dissertation research activities. A review of the range of topics that fall under the umbrella of cultural heritage and a review of theory and practice in one or more of these topics. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Research Design & Proposal Preparation
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to graduate students in Anthropology. Covers the development of anthropological research designs and proposals. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Cultural Heritage Policy & Practice
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. Restricted to graduate students in Anthropology. Exploration of critical issues in cultural heritage policy emphasizing the regulatory basis for federal CRM, public anthropology, and indigenous people's issues. Hands-on training in the design and production of federal planning documents. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Advanced Research
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered every term. Directed individual research and study appropriate to the background and objectives of the student. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Seminar in Cultural Heritage
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: ANTY
courses.title: Dissertation
courses.desc: (R-10) Offered every term. Doctoral dissertation research activities. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: AASC
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. This course brings students the opportunity to learn Arabic via a communicative approach, where the emphasis is placed on the functional use of the Arabic Language. Active skills are listening, speaking, reading, and writing, plus basic cultural study.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., ARAB 101. A continuation of ARAB 101. Students learn Arabic via a communicative approach, where the emphasis is placed on the functional use of the Arabic Language. Active skills are listening, speaking, reading, and writing, plus basic cultural study.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one–time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ARAB 102. This course is designed to help students further develop their language skills (listening, speaking, reading, and writing) and learn more about Arab culture and advanced grammar rules beyond the elementary level. The target proficiency level is intermediate-low/mid based on proficiency guidelines from the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., ARAB 201. This course is a continuation of ARAB 201. It is designed to help students further develop their language skills (listening, speaking, reading, and writing) and learn more about the Arab culture and advanced grammar rules beyond the elementary level. The target proficiency level is intermediate-mid based on proficiency guidelines from the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one–time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Advanced Modern Standard Arabic I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ARAB 202. This course is designed to help students further develop their language skills (listening, speaking, reading, and writing) and learn more about Arab culture and advanced grammar rules beyond the intermediate level. The target proficiency level is intermediate-high based on proficiency guidelines from the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Advanced Modern Standard Arabic II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., ARAB 301. This course is a continuation of ARAB 301. It is designed to help students further develop their language skills (listening, speaking, reading, and writing) and learn more about Arab culture and advanced grammar rules beyond the intermediate level. The target proficiency level is intermediate-high/advanced-low based on proficiency guidelines from the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: The Arab World
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Students explore the Arabic-speaking countries through in-depth discussions of their history, geography, peoples, economy, political systems, educational systems, and cultural components, such as music, cuisine, tradition, customs, gender relations, etc. This course is designed for everyone interested in the topic, and no previous knowledge of the Arabic language is required.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Media, Culture, and Society in the Arab World
courses.desc: This course explores the relationship between media, culture, and society across the Arab world from the early 20th century to the present. Students examine how newspapers, radio, film, television, and digital platforms shape cultural expression, public debate, and social change. Through analysis of films, news reports, popular music, satire, and contemporary social media, students consider how narratives about gender, identity, religion, politics, and globalization circulate within and beyond the region. Emphasis is placed on interpreting cultural and media artifacts as sources that reflect and reshape Arab societies. This course develops skills in critical interpretation, cross-cultural analysis, and evidence-based argumentation. Taught in English; no prior knowledge of Arabic required.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Conflict and Diplomacy in the Arab World
courses.desc: This course examines how culture, identity, and communication shape conflict and diplomacy across the Arab world. Students explore key regional conflicts and peacebuilding efforts from historical, political, and cultural perspectives, focusing on how language, religion, media, and social norms influence negotiation and international engagement. Topics include the Arab-Israeli conflict, Gulf diplomacy, the role of the Arab League, media and war coverage, humanitarian crises, and regional peace initiatives. Through case studies, simulations, and analysis of diplomatic documents and news reports, students evaluate how actors—states, NGOs, journalists, and international institutions—frame, interpret, and attempt to resolve conflict. The course emphasizes ethical reasoning, evidence-based analysis, and intercultural communication. Taught in English; no prior knowledge of Arabic required.

courses.subject: ARAB

courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one–time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ARAB
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Visual Language - Drawing
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to basic drawing skills and concept integration. Studio practice with research in historical and contemporary approaches.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Visual Language - 3-D Foundations
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to the formal elements and principles of design in 3-D.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Ceramics for Non-majors
courses.desc: Offered Offered autumn and spring. A general introduction to ceramics for non-art majors. Learn a variety of techniques working with clay and glazes. No Art experience required. Not for B.A, B.F.A majors or art minors.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings by visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, and/or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Drawing I
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., ARTZ 105A. Study of human anatomy through drawing, in-class skills development, homework portfolio, and research in historical and contemporary figuration required.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Illustration
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ARTZ 105A. This course is an introduction to drawing techniques as they pertain to the commercial illustration industry; emphasis on creative interpretation and disciplined draftsmanship for the visual communication of ideas.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Painting I
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., ARTZ 105A. Introduction to acrylic and oil painting. Emphasis on color theory, composition, concept development, and research in historical and contemporary strategies.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Ceramics I
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to ceramic techniques. Introduction to clay as a historical and contemporary medium to explore art making. Emphasis on handbuilding and wheel throwing, and concept development including large scale sculpture and functional pottery.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Sculpture I
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to fundamental technical skills and processes used to make sculptural objects. Emphasis on formal concerns, concept development, and new technologies in art.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Printmaking I
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Emphasis on multiples, layering color, and collaboration. Topics may include: relief, intaglio, lithography, screenprinting, artist books, mixed media, or photo-processes. Consideration of historical and contemporary approaches.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Photography I: Technologies and Processes
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to photography. Emphasis on exposure, digital camera basics, composition, digital photography processing, and print finishing techniques. Consideration of historical and contemporary approaches.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings by visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, and/or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Teaching Early Childhood and Elementary Art
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, and Art Education. This is a general teaching methods course in visual art education. This course is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the roles, values, classroom pedagogy, and current issues in P-8 visual art education; to investigate child development; to offer an introduction to content standards; and to examine a broad array of art education theories and practices. Students are introduced to available curriculum resources and will engage in academic service learning.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Drawing II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Prereq., ARTZ 211A. Focus on integrating content and form in drawings and research in historical and contemporary ideas.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Environmental Drawing
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Open to students in the Wilderness and Civilization program (Wilderness Studies minor) during fall semesters. Open to all students during spring semester. Exploration and production of drawings, with an emphasis on an environmental context; studio practicum, lectures, critiques, reading and writing required. Some restrictions might be applied to specific sections of this course.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Painting II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., ARTZ 221A. Continued development of painting skills and concepts with an emphasis on contemporary ideas and approaches. Topics may include: figuration, place, process, abstraction, and other contemporary themes.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Ceramics II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., ARTZ 231A. More advanced development of ceramic process with emphasis on idea development and individual skill building. Depending on the section handbuilding, wheel throwing and other technique will be taught. Focus on integrating content and form through study of historical and contemporary approaches.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Ceramics Surfaces
courses.desc: Offered autumn. In-depth study of the physical and chemical properties of clays and glazes. Hands-on testing of clay and glaze formulas and introduction to kiln ﬁring.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Sculpture II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Continued development of sculptural processes. Emphasis on clear sculptural responses to material-based and topic-based assignments. Consideration of both analog and digital means. Topics may include fabrication, foundry, fiber, and other materials and approaches.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Printmaking II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Continued development of printmaking processes. Emphasis on integration of content. Focus on layering of color, increased scale, styles of format and presentation, and research in historical and contemporary approach topics may include: relief, screenprinting, monotypes, book arts, and outsourced digital fabrication methods.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Analog Photography
courses.desc: Prereq., ARTZ 284A or JRNL 257A. This is an exploration of analog photographic techniques and methods employing light-sensitive film and paper as well as using a variety of different camera systems and film formats. The course emphasizes advancement of technical control and darkroom experimentation resulting in students establishing individual portfolios. A 35 mm film camera is required for this class.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Photography II: Theory, Criticism, and Practice
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., ARTZ 284A or JRNL 257A. Further exploration of digital photography. Emphasis on effective use of color, advanced camera operation and image editing techniques with software and image output, studio and strobe lighting. Emphasis on content development, technical knowledge, presentation, and research in historical and contemporary approaches.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Synthesis
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., or corequisite ARTZ 380. This course allows students to draw together their learning and their critical thinking into a defining experience, through the development of a synthesis project and a written presentation.

courses.desc: (R-12) Supervised, practical experience in a professional setting relevant to the student's field of study.

Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Teaching Art I - K-12
courses.desc: Offered fall. Restricted to Art majors. This course is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the roles, values, classroom pedagogy, and current issues in K-12 visual art education; to investigate child development; to offer an introduction to content standards; and to examine a broad array of art education theories and practices. Students are introduced to curriculum resources and will engage in academic service learning. Level: Undergraduate/Graduate

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Teaching Art II - K-12
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., ARTZ 402. Restricted to Art majors. Continuation and practical application of ARTZ 402. Level: Undergraduate/Graduate

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Advanced Research- Ceramics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Prereq., ARTZ 231A. An advanced critique-based studio class where students design their own project proposals and work one-on-one with the faculty. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Technology Design for Interactive and Installation Art
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered fall. Restricted to students in the College of Arts and Media with at least junior standing. Students work across multiple disciplines and media to create art installations. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Socially Engaged Art
courses.desc: (R-9) This course explores the evolving field of socially engaged art—a practice grounded in collaboration, participation, and dialogue. Students will examine the historical and theoretical foundations of socially engaged practice, study its principles and ethics, and consider the role of personal identity in shaping meaningful work. Through a combination of studio production, service-learning, readings, and critical discussion, students will design and implement projects that engage with communities and address social issues. While centered on making, the course emphasizes research, reflection, and exchange as essential components of practice. Ideal for students interested in expanding the boundaries of art, this course offers opportunities to merge creative work with social impact and contribute to collective cultural conversations. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.desc: (R-12) Independent research under the direction of a faculty member. Level: undergraduate.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Seminar- Professional Practices
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ARTH 250L. Restricted to students with senior standing. Required of all graduating B.F.A. students. Introduction to professional practices and standards in the visual arts, including: presentation, portfolio development, career and exhibition opportunities, arts advocacy, and graduate school application. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ARTZ
courses.title: Senior Studio Project
courses.desc: Offered spring. Capstone studio class of a self-determined ambitious thesis project. Specific projects formats are determined individually and include thematic integration. courses.desc: Surveys world art from prehistory through the present day with the objective of developing a critical understanding of art forms in their historical and cultural context.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art of World Civilization: 1400 to Present
courses.desc: Offered spring. Survey of the history of visual art from 1400 to the present.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Art Criticism
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., WRIT 101 or WRIT 201; and ARTH 150H. Study of the description, interpretation, and evaluation of visual art as practiced in art criticism.

courses.subject: ARTH

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Architectural History I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., ARTH 150H or ARTH 201H. Exploration of architectural styles, designs, and choices of the built environment from prehistory to the modern age.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Architectural History II
courses.desc: Prereq., ARTH 201H and ARTH 250L. Exploration of architectural styles, designs, and choices of the built environment from 1850 to the present.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Edconic: Contemporary Art & Global Feminisms
courses.desc: Offered every semester. Restricted to students in the Edconic program. Taught at Sotheby's Institute in London by Edconic instructors. This course will consider the key global currents of fifty years of feminist art around a number of themes. These include feminist art about the body and sexuality, women's domestic labour, feminist approaches to identity, motherhood and childcare, violence against women, feminism, and the art historical canon. Students will encounter these themes through a number of different media, from painting, photography and sculpture to textile, digital, and performance art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Edconic: Hogarth to Himid: Histories of British Art
courses.desc: Offered every semester. Restricted to students in the Edconic program. Taught at Sotheby's Institute in London by Edconic instructors. This course provides a survey of British art spanning from the 17th century to the present day, introducing students to artworks, artists, and significant collections of British art. In the breadth of art and artists studied, there will be particular attention given to Black and multicultural British art and women artists who have been less visible in canonical surveys of British art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Edconic: Curator Academy
courses.desc: Offered every semester. Restricted to students in the Edconic program. Taught at Sotheby's Institute in London Edconic instructors. This course surveys current developments in curating art, examining expanded definitions of curating (in museums and independently post-2020), and the evolving local, global, and digital landscapes for curatorial work and activity today.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Edconic: The Global Art Market
courses.desc: Offered every semester. Restricted to students in the Edconic program. Taught at Sotheby's Institute in London by Edconic instructors. This course explores the emergence and key concepts of the global market for art from the 18th to the 21st centuries through a discussion of its history, disruptions and innovations. The course takes a thematic approach delivered via specific case studies to map the key concepts, individuals and institutions, and the various business models, and ethical and legal considerations that underpin the contemporary market.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Edconic: Exploring Collections, Exploding Canons
courses.desc: Offered every semester. Restricted to students in the Edconic program. Taught at Sotheby's Institute in London by Edconic instructors. This course introduces and examines London's internationally significant museum and gallery collections from a critical and global perspective. Exploring the politics of collecting and display, it engages with contemporary art historical and curatorial debates via the realities of institutions and their collections - and the inherent tensions therein.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Contemporary Art and Art Criticism
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., WRIT 101 or WRIT 201; and ARTH 250L. Exploration of artists, art works, critics, and theories from 1960 to the present.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Manga and Anime: History, Practice, and Form
courses.desc: Surveys the history and genres of Japanese comics (manga) and animation (anime). Students will learn how to analyze/draw the visual elements of manga and anime while also learning about cultural context, production, and reception. In addition to discussing common themes and narrative forms employed, students will learn to distinguish among, describe, and draw the various art styles and framing structures.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings by visiting professors, new courses, and/or one-time investigations of current topics.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Visualizing Climate Change in Art, Film, and Media
courses.desc: It is difficult to see climate. Despite this challenge, scientists, artists, and designers have developed various materials and methods to help visualize climate in parts and fragments and through the creation of new types of experience. This course investigates how art, film, and digital media represent and engage with ecological themes, climate-related issues, and other hard-to-see things on a global scale within the context of environmental history and contemporary eco-scholarship in the humanities. The class will include field trips, interviews, and other local site visits. As a final project, students will produce a creative proposal for bringing greater visibility to a local climate-related topic.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: 20th Century Art
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., ARTH 150H or ARTH 201H and ARTH 250L. Exploration of art and architecture of the 20th century. Level: undergraduate and graduate.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Open Range: Land Art and the American Consciousness
courses.desc: Offered spring. The aim of this course is to investigate the sense of place in American visual arts of the 19th to 21st centuries. The course provides a roughly chronological view of the development of place in the American landscape, particularly in the west, and how that has been articulated by visual artists. Level: undergraduate.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: History of Photography
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., ARTH 150H or 201H and ARTH 250L. Exploration of the history of photography from the early 19th century to the 21st century. Level: undergraduate.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: History of Time-Based Arts
courses.desc: Time-based art and media—including video, performance, and software-based art—play a major role in modern and contemporary art practice. This course charts how, since the 19th century, time-based art and media have shattered categories between art, science, and technology and collapsed distinctions between artists and viewers as well as artists and machines. Alongside these categorical shifts, the concept of time has been pursued as a topic worthy of artistic exploration as both a theme and structuring principle. Into this century, time-based art and media continue to provoke important questions for artists, curators, and conservators, among others. These questions include: How can impermanent works be preserved? Should curators migrate artworks to new formats as technologies evolve? And how can artists both critique and repurpose commercial media within their practice? Level: Undergradaute

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Surrealism
courses.desc: This course explores surrealism as a revolt against socially-constructed reality itself. Students will explore primary works from ancient Greek poetry to Lautréamont's absurd chants and Breton’s 1924 Manifesto. Emphasis is placed on overlooked figures, obscure texts, and the movement’s continual alignment with wide-ranging paradigms of human experience and cultural expression. Readings and screenings reveal Surrealism's importance as an unfinished, disobedient practice that continues to unsettle contemporary theoretical models. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The History of Body & Performance Art
courses.desc: This course examines body and performance art as a persistent challenge to the boundaries of art, identity, and social order. Students will study works ranging from early ritual and avant-garde practices to radical experiments of the 20th century and into contemporary global performance. Emphasis is placed on overlooked artists, ephemeral gestures, and the stakes of embodiment in diverse cultural, social, and historical contexts. Readings, screenings, and live documentation highlight performance’s role as a disruptive, unfinished practice that continually redefines the relation between artist, audience, and society. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Gallery Practices & Management
courses.desc: This course is one part experiential learning with hands-on work in the Gallery of Arts and one part lecture, assignment, and discussion. The course will introduce knowledge about exhibition design, a range of art gallery business models, and arts administration operations including non-profit organizations. Students will also learn historical and contemporary approaches to curatorial practices and relate ethics to curating. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.title: Planetary Astronomy
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Students should have taken high school algebra and geometry prior to registration. An introduction to observational, historical, and planetary astronomy. Students will have a chance to visit UM's state-of-the-art planetarium and observe with our 0.4 meter telescope.

courses.desc: Offered spring. Students should have taken high school algebra and geometry prior to registration. An introduction to stars, stellar evolution, galaxies, and cosmology. Students will have a chance to visit UM’s state-of-the-art planetarium and observe with our 0.4 meter telescope.
