courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Game Programming
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., CSCI 151. Introduction to game programming with an emphasis on algorithms, data structures, and networking. This course introduces students to the Godot engine and the algorithms and data structures needed to create highly optimized and functional games. Students will explore the technologies behind game networking and how to design multiplayer connections.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computers, Ethics, and Society
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., WRIT 101 and CSCI 151. Restricted to Computer Science majors. Ethical problems that computer scientists face. The codes of ethics of professional computing societies. The social implications of computers, computing, and other digital technologies

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Web Application Development
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 258. This course imparts advanced web development and associated practical skills, including contemporary web architectures, cloud deployment, database migrations, custom front end interfaces, high performance computing integration, web systems debugging, and group development.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Software Science
courses.desc: Offered fall. Prereq., CSCI 152. Study, implementation, and assessment of software processes, techniques, methods, and CASE tools. Project management and cost estimation techniques will be examined. A group project may be required.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., CSCI 232 and M 225. Algorithm design, analysis, and correctness. Covers algorithm design techniques such as greedy, divide and conquer, and dynamic programming, and advanced graph algorithms. Introduces the classes P and NP.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Database Design
courses.desc: Offered fall. Prereq., CSCI 232. Fundamentals of data modeling, the relational mode, normal forms, file organization, index structures and SQL. Major project involving the design and implementation of a relational database.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Mobile Application Development
courses.desc: Offered fall. Prereq., CSCI 152 and CSCI 258. This course introduces the process of developing mobile applications. It is well suited to students with experience writing programs using an object-oriented programming language such as Java and who have experience working with basic data structures. This course will focus on creating user interfaces and program logic for a variety of different applications.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 152. Bottom up creation of a complete computer system. Beginning with logic gates, ALU, CPU, and memory hierarchy. Instruction set design and hardware control. Assembly language and creation of an assembler. Virtual machines and implementation of a virtual machine. High level languages and basic compiler construction.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Sports Analytics
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to students with at least junior standing. This course will discuss how technology is affecting sports and the ethical consequences. Students will be introduced to several computer science topics that are used to analyze all aspects of the sports industry, including performance, safety, game strategy, and the fan experience.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Research
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Directed individual research and study appropriate to the background and objectives of the student.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Restricted to students with at least junior standing. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation. Graded CR/NCR only.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Geospatial Data Science
courses.desc: Prereq., CSCI 151 with a grade of B or better and one of M 162, M 171, or STAT 216. Data scientists often need to incorporate geospatial knowledge into workflows and geographic information system (GIS) professionals need to incorporate data science methods into theirs. This class is targeted at both populations, stressing the knowledge and skills required for success, eg data types, projections, coordinate reference planes, GIS systems, remote sensing, the Python geospatial analysis tool chain, assessing geospatial spatial correlation, geospatial predictive modeling using machine learning. Level: Undergraduate
courses.prereq: CSCI 151 with a grade of B or better and one of M 162, M 171, or STAT 216

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Careers in Computer Science
courses.desc: Prereq., CSCI 426. This course should be taken in the student's final year of the degree. This course is designed to equip graduating computer science students with the essential skills and strategies to successfully navigate the job market. It includes career development activities, interview preparation, and professional guidance. For those interested in continuing their education, this course also provides insights into preparing strong graduate school applications. A comprehensive program assessment exam will also be administered in this course. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Software Engineering
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 258 and CSCI 332. This course focuses on both foundational and contemporary practices of software engineering with a special emphasis on design patterns. It blends theory with hands-on practice, equipping students with a comprehensive understanding of advanced software design and development methodologies. As software systems continue to evolve, mastering these time-tested techniques becomes essential to create efficient, scalable, and maintainable software. Beyond design patterns, this course delves into object-oriented, the Unified Modeling Language (UML), software testing, collaborative software engineering, and a host of other software engineering principles. Co-convenes with CSCI 523. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Software Design & Development I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., CSCI 322, CSCI 323, and CSCI 340. Restricted to students with senior standing. Class represents first in senior capstone experience. Students will work in groups to design and prototype real-world software. Focus will be on client interaction, software engineering methodologies, project management tools, requirements specification and analysis, design, user feedback, documentation and presentation. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Software Design and Development II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 426. Design and implementation of a major software project in a group setting, with required documentation, presentation, installation, and approval by the instructor. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Algorithm Topics
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., M 221 and CSCI 332 with a minimum grade of B-. Covers theory of computing and an instructor-selected set of advanced algorithms topics, such as approximation algorithms, randomized algorithms, parallel algorithms, streaming algorithms, linear programming, cryptography, quantum computing, etc. Co-Convenes with CSCI 532. Level: Undergraduate
courses.prereq: M 221 and CSCI 332 with a minimum grade of B-

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: User Interface Design
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., CSCI 232. Introduction to usability and key concepts of human behavior. Focus on the process of user-centered design, including requirements specification, prototyping, and methods of evaluation. Incorporation of regular design critiques of classmates' work, and emphasis on both oral and written communication skills. Co-convenes with CSCI 543. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Data Visualization
courses.desc: Offered fall. Restricted to students with at least junior status. Programming experience is necessary for success in this course. This course emphasizes the practice of data visualization, compelling students to identify and master tools to produce visualizations of data having relational, raster, vector, geographical, networked, mesh based, spectral, or phase space properties. The unique challenges of each data type will be covered. The emphasis on production is coupled to a framework for critique, allowing students to differentiate between high and low qualities visualizations. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., CSCI 232. Introduction to the framework of learning from examples, various learning algorithms such as neural networks, and generic learning principles such as inductive bias, Occam's Razor, and data mining. Co-convenes with CSCI 547. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 232. Covers several areas in which the brain has become better understood through computation (vision, learning, and memory). This course provides an introduction to cognitive neuroscience as well as basic computational methods. We will use Python and focus on ‘open science’ practice. Co-convenes with CSCI 550. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computational Biology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Designed for attendance by both computer scientists and biologists. The course will explore the interdisciplinary nature at the juncture of the two fields. Students will be introduced to bioinformatics (emphasis: computational genomics), with exposure to fundamental problems, algorithms, and tools in the field. This includes a basic introduction to genomics, along with in-depth coverage of algorithms and methods relevant to modern computational genomics, including: biological sequence alignment, sequence database homology search, and phylogeny inference. The programming expectations are limited for a 400-level computer science course, but at least one semester of a programming-intensive course is required. Co-convenes with CSCI 558. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Embedded Systems
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 232. Students are expected to have knowledge of computer architecture and operating systems and an experience with at least one programming language, such as Python or C. This course is designed to bring students to the design, implement, and evaluate embedded systems. Such systems usually include four main components: data collection, data processing, data communication, and adaptive control. In that, the data collection includes hardware and software to control embedded sensors to “sense” the information and report to host computer. Data processing includes a set of methods to remove noises from the raw data and only maintain the information of interested. Data communication includes hardware and software to exchange data between embedded controllers, sensors, and host machine (e.g., Bluetooth or Wi-Fi). Finally, yet importantly, adaptive control includes a set of algorithms provides the “act” to the system according to the input data. In this class, students will have opportunity to walk through all the components mentioned earlier and have a capability of design and implement a small cyber-physical project by the end of the semester. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 232. Operating system design principles. Processes, threads, synchronization, deadlock, memory management, file management and file systems, protection, and security, comparison of commonly used existing operating systems, writing programs that make use of operating system services. It is recommended, but not required, that the student also attend Programming Languages (in order to be prepared to write C programs) and Architecture (in order to understand interactions between the operating system and processor hardware) prior to attending this course. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Internet of Things
courses.desc: Prereq., CSCI 232. Students are expected to have experience with at least one programming language prior to registration. Wireless and mobile systems have become ubiquitous. They are playing a significant role in our everyday life nowadays. However, the increasing demand for wireless connectivity and the emergence of new areas such as the Internet of Things present new research challenges. This course will introduce the spectrum of research on the Internet of Things (IoT). The lectures cover a range of techniques in sensing, computing, communication, and wireless networking and connect them to various applications in analytics, localization, cyber-physical systems, mobile health, security, and wearables. Co-convenes with CSCI 561. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Networks
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., CSCI 232. Concepts and practice of computer networking, network protocol layers, switching, routing, flow, and congestion control. Network programming. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Security
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., M 225. Introduction to computer security. Understand the basis of cryptography and secure systems, as well as exploits used to penetrate such systems. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Simulation
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., M 172 or CSCI 151. Matrix languages. ODE solving; Euler-Richardson, Runge-Kutta, PDE solving; finite differences, finite elements, multi-grid techniques. Discrete methods for solution, renormalization group method, critical phenomena. Emphasis on presentation of results and interactive programs. Co-convenes with CSCI 577. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: High Performance Computing
courses.desc: Prereq., CSCI 232. This course covers techniques for using modern computing hardware to tackle complex problems in the sciences, machine learning, and data science. Topics include numerical libraries, multi-threading, parallel processing, GPU programming, profiling, checkpointing, and the use of clusters and cloud computing. Level: Undergraduate

courses.desc: (R-6) Offered every term. Senior thesis for computer science majors and/or Watkins scholars. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Graduate Research Methods
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Development of the skills required for effective research in Computer Science, including literature review, research proposal development, oral and visual presentation techniques. Included is mandatory attendance of a colloquium featuring presentations from UM faculty and students as well as external researchers from academics and industry. Level: Graduate

courses.desc: Offered spring. Advanced algorithm and data structure concepts, including theory, approximation algorithms, randomized algorithms, parallel algorithms, streaming algorithms, linear programming. Co-Convenes with CSCI 432. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Human-Computer Interaction
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Principles of good design for interactive systems and web-based applications. User-centered design methodology including requirements specification, low and high-fidelity prototyping, heuristic evaluation, cognitive walkthrough, predictive modeling, and usability testing. Advanced HCI research project. Co-convenes with CSCI 443. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Fundamentals of machine learning including neural networks, decision trees, Bayesian learning, instance-based learning, and genetic algorithms; inductive bias, Occam's razor, and learning theory; data mining; software agents. Co-convenes with CSCI 447. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., CSCI 547. This course is a survey of state-of-the-art methods in deep learning. Covered topics are expected to change, but will typically include convolutional and recurrent neural networks, transformers, automatic differentiation, uncertainty quantification, generative models, deep reinforcement learning, training parallelism, model distillation, and interesting applications of all of the above to scientific problems. Students will read primary literature, present it to their peers, and develop computational implementations. Level: Graduate

courses.title: Intro to Bioinformatics

A substantial project is a key component of the course. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Introduction to Woodworking
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered at Missoula College. In this course, students will learn the foundational skills required to complete basic woodworking projects, including wood species identification and characteristics, appropriate use of essential shop tools, and shop safety. This course is a prerequisite for all higher-level woodworking offerings.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Joinery
courses.desc: (R-2) Prereq., CSTN 105. Building on foundational skills learned in CSTN 105 (Introduction to Woodworking), students will advance their skills in basic woodworking and learn additional methods of wood shaping and joinery to be able to complete more complex woodworking projects. Sample topics include lumber selection and preparation, glue-up techniques, mortise and tenon joints, dovetails, and wood finishing.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Intermediate Woodworking
courses.desc: (R-2) Prereq., CSTN 105 and CSTN 107. Students will learn and demonstrate more advanced woodworking skills through the completion of in-shop projects. Building on skills and techniques learned in CSTN 105 and CSTN 107, students will complete their own woodworking project from start to finish, from project design, material selection and estimating, wood selection and preparation, through final finishing. This course is intended to provide an opportunity for practice and refinement of advanced woodworking skills through actual project completion.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Carpentry Basics & Rough-In Framing
courses.desc: Coreq., CSTN 122. This is an introductory course in residential carpentry and rough framing. Students will be introduced to the essential tools, materials, fasteners, and techniques used in basic residential framing. Students will learn how to safely operate hand and power tools, read construction drawings, and apply fundamental carpentry skills in the construction of floor, wall, and roof systems. Students will complete a series of hands-on projects, including participating in the rough framing of a complete single-family home.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Carpentry Basics and Rough Framing Lab
courses.desc: Coreq., CSTN 120. This course is a hands-on lab designed to support and apply the concepts introduced in CSTN 120. Students will participate in guided lab activities focused on safe tool use, basic framing, material handling, and construction techniques.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Interior & Exterior Finish Carpentry
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Study of various types of siding, gutter systems, roof venting requirements, and framing with metal studs. Installation of sheathing, exterior siding, roofing felt, shingles, insulation vapor barriers, and stairs on small building constructed in CSTN 120. Installation of wood and metal doors. Demonstration of materials, layout and installation of suspended ceilings. Selection and installation of countertops, base cabinets and wall cabinets. Window, door, floor, ceiling trim and drywall are installed in a small building. This course includes a one-credit imbedded lab.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Intermediate Carpentry Lab
courses.desc: Prereq., CSTN 120 and CSTN 122. Offered at Missoula College. Lab to accompany CSTN 142.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Drywall Lab
courses.desc: This course covers the most common systems of interior wall assemblies and finishes for residential construction, including air sealing, insulation, and wall coverings. The course will provide an overview of materials and techniques for completing the interior of residential walls and covers material selection, estimating, and installation techniques of the most common wall finishes. Students will work towards completing drywall hanging, seam taping, and basic texturing over both wood framed and steel framed walls.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Site Prep, Foundation, and Concrete Installation
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Introduces the process of distance measurement as well as differential and trigonometric leveling for site layout. It covers the principles, equipment, and methods used to perform the site layout tasks that require making angular measurements. This course is designed to let students apply the blueprint reading skills learned so far to a practical exercise.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Residential Building Codes and Inspection
courses.desc: This course is an entry level course designed to expose the student to residential building codes and the inspection process in Missoula County. The focus of this course is to interpret and understand the building codes and inspection processes relevant to the building phases of one- and two-family residential dwellings. This course is 80% lecture and 20% self-paced student projects.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Advanced Carpentry Lecture
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, and CSTN 143. Study of the process for angular measurement, using transits, theodolites, electronic distance measuring devices, lasers, and trigonometric calculating to lay out foundations and determine elevations. Installation of standing seam, lap seam, and built-up roofing systems; concrete, vinyl, wooden, tile, and carpeted floors as well as radiant heating; paneling, wainscoting, movable partitions, curtain walls and fire-rated commercial wall construction. Advanced stair systems, including shop built and prefabricated stairs, balustrades, mitered risers and treads, and layout of elliptical fastening methods, and assembly techniques. Project planning, scheduling, estimating, and management skills included. This course includes a two-credit lab.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Advanced Carpentry Lab
courses.desc: Prereq., CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, and CSTN 143. Offered at Missoula College. Laboratory to accompany CSTN 205.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Residential Construction Estimating
courses.desc: This is an introductory course in residential project estimating. Students will be asked to formulate spreadsheets and will learn how to apply costs to labor, materials, and equipment in residential construction projects, how to do material take-offs and quantify construction projects, and will prepare a bid as part of a project.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Building Management
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, CSTN 143, and CSTN 171. Introduction to building business and project management including overhead costs, payroll costs, estimating and scheduling. Covers elements of payroll computation and preparation, payroll tax returns, information returns, and identification and compensation of independent contractors. Students are introduced to building cost estimating, and scheduling of subcontractors and building inspections. This course includes a one-credit imbedded lab.
courses.prereq: CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, CSTN 143, and CSTN 171

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Applied Building Practices Lab
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, CSTN 143. Students work on a variety of projects either at the college or in the community to practice and develop their skills as well as learn new skills. Knowing and following OSHA rules and regulations is emphasized. Students are expected to produce a professional quality product.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Commercial Construction
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, CSTN 143, and CSTN 171. Study and develop skills in metal stud framing, commercial roofing systems, metal and masonry buildings, metal doors and door hardware, suspended ceilings, and fire rated commercial walls.
courses.prereq: CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, CSTN 143, and CSTN 171

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Project Scheduling for Residential Construction
courses.desc: Offered at Missoula College. This course is an introductory course designed to teach residential construction project scheduling. Heavy emphasis is on project sequencing and a study of conventional scheduling using the critical path method, precedence networks, bar charts, monthly reports, and fast track scheduling. Students will work to understand and apply the available methods of project scheduling, including sequencing of different construction processes as well as formulating and diagramming schedules.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Green Building Concept & Design I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. This course takes a holistic approach to natural resource conservation and energy efficiency in the construction industry. From integrated design, building site selection and evaluation, through building design, material selection and efficiencies, passive heating and cooling, and construction techniques. Students design an energy efficient residence to be built by next years class.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Green Building Concept & Design II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., CSTN 282. A course fee of $50.00 is required. This course builds on concepts learned in CSTN 282 Green Building Concepts and Design I. Students learn how to weatherize existing buildings and green remodeling and preservation techniques, design and build outdoor living spaces, and green landscaping practices. They learn how to document building for green rating for both NAHB Standards and LEED. They will conduct blower door tests and learn to test for and mitigate radon gas. Students will also refine the energy efficient residential plan they produced in Green Building Concepts and Design I.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Advanced Wood Buildings
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Curriculum will provide current and future industry participants education in the history, benefits, sourcing, design, products, applications and techniques in modern and emerging wood and wood frame construction. It will further showcase the inherent qualities of responsibly sourced wood as a rapidly renewable resource in single family residential, low rise multifamily, mixed use commercial and high rise buildings and inform both current practitioners and future industry workforce members on the products, techniques and tools in wood building construction that provide the maximum economic and sustainable benefits.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Practicum
courses.desc: (R-3) Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. The course will be an elective for all students within the Sustainable Construction Technology Program and a requirement for any student pursuing a CTS in Green Building. The practicum will allow students to apply concepts learned in CSTN 282 Green Building and Design I, CSTN 283 Green Building and Design II, and CSTN 261 Building Management in a hands on project, research activity or other relevant designated undertaking.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Construction Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Extended classroom experience which provides practical application of classroom learning. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: CSTN
courses.title: Capstone: Carpentry
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Capstone laboratory to accompany CSTN 120, CSTN 122, CSTN 142, CSTN 143, CSTN 205, CSTN 206, and CSTN 261. This course provides hands-on experience in which the student applies the skills and knowledge presented in the Carpentry Program. The course will emphasize advanced application in the areas of exterior finishing and interior finishing, and other constructed topics.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Intimate Relationships
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring semester. This course covers the fascinating, multi-faceted world of intimate relationships and explores the topic from empirical and theoretical perspectives. The examination of intimate relationships in this course will look at the subject through cultural, biological, social and developmental lenses and will explore specific topics such as attraction, communication, friendship, sexuality, love, conflict, power and violence, loss, social cognition, and repairing relationships.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.desc: (R-6) Independent research under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Forgiveness & Reconciliation
courses.desc: Offered spring. Survey of the theory and practice of healing fractured relationships at the individual and community levels, treating historical and personal issues from philosophical, psychological and religious perspectives drawn from several diverse cultures. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: Undergraduate and Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Introduction to Counseling
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. This course is designed to prepare school and mental health counselors-in-training gain an understanding of the counseling field and begin developing professional identity. Much of the material introduced in this course will be developed in greater detail in later courses. This course is an overview that prepares the student for their professional identity and activities. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Theories & Techniques of Counseling
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Examination of historic and current theories of counseling. Overview of techniques associated with each theory. Basic introduction to ethical concerns with each theory. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Counseling Fundamentals
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Overview of approaches to counseling, including common factors. Includes meta-theoretical considerations and guided dyadic practice. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Group Counseling & Guidance
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Theories, approaches, and methods for group counseling and guidance. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Applied Counseling Skills
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., COUN 511 and COUN 512. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Review and application of counseling theories and techniques to client issues. Intensive supervision including ethics, professional practice and diagnostic considerations. Lecture and class presentation with a focus on professional counseling development. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Individual Appraisal
courses.desc: Offered summer. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Overview of appraisal techniques utilized in counseling, including interviewing, observation, and psychological/educational testing. The processes of selection, administration, scoring, interpretation, and reporting information from appraisal techniques are examined in relation to practical, legal, and ethical considerations. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Counseling Research & Program Evaluation
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. This course provides an overview and analysis of quantitative and qualitative research approaches used within the professional counseling discipline. A focus on understanding key research concepts (e.g., internal validity, external validity) within the context of contemporary research publications in counseling is emphasized. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Introduction to Family Counseling
courses.desc: Offered fall. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. An introduction to the major theories, techniques, and diagnostic tools of family counseling. Course includes a family systems emphasis. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Risk & Resiliency
courses.desc: Offered fall. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. This course is a required course in the graduate Department of Counseling's Clinical Mental Health Counseling and School Counseling programs.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Lifespan Developmental Counseling
courses.desc: Offered summer. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Overview of counseling from the framework of lifespan developmental theory. Normal and abnormal development in the environmental context of family, school, society and culture is emphasized. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: School Counseling, Program Development, & Supervision
courses.desc: Offered fall. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Examination of counseling techniques and approaches relevant to prevention and remediation of behavioral, social, emotional and academic problems for students P-12. Overview of school counseling program development and administration. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Counseling Children & Adolescents
courses.desc: Offered every spring. Prereq., COUN 511 and COUN 512. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Review and application of counseling concerns and approaches with children and adolescents in school and related educational settings, including classroom and psychoeducational strategies. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Career Counseling Theory & Technology
courses.desc: Offered summer only. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Examination of theories of career choice and development; information sources for career counseling; techniques and approaches of career counseling with clients at different stages of career and life development and from diverse populations. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Multicultural Counseling
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. An introduction to the field of multicultural counseling. Issues and practical considerations in counseling five population groups; definition of terms and concepts. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Counseling Methods: School & Agency
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered every term. Prereq., COUN 511, COUN 512, and COUN 530. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Supervised counseling methods and theories as applied in mental health agencies and schools. Review of the principles of counseling as these apply to various settings and client issues. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Comprehensive Project
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Integration of professional experience and academic research in a comprehensive paper or applied project. Students may elect to have an oral examination covering the eight CACREP core areas of counseling. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Research
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Directed individual research and study appropriate to the background and objectives of the student. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-24) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Requires consent of instructor. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Group analysis of problems in specific areas of professional counseling. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Practical application of classroom learning in off-campus placements. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Professional Ethics and Orientation
courses.desc: Offered fall. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. The public and institutional roles and responsibilities of counseling professionals including ethical and legal responsibilities. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Diagnosis/Treatment Planning in Counseling
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Overview of diagnosis, treatment planning and case documentation in counseling. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Advanced Counseling Theories
courses.desc: Prereq., COUN 511. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. This course provides an overview and analysis of evidence based treatments in counseling. There is a focus on cognitive-behavioral treatments for specific disorders as well as acceptance and commitment therapy and principles of evidence-based relationships. Practical application of these approaches is emphasized. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Introduction to Mental Health Systems
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Essential knowledge for professional identity, understanding of public policy, and community assessment procedures. Includes brief lectures, guest speakers, discussion, and student presentations. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Doctoral Clinical Practice
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Doctoral level clinical experience of 100 supervised hours focusing on the counseling relationship, including case conceptualization and therapeutic skills from a variety of theoretical perspectives. Additional areas of focus are ethical considerations and the assessment of professional counseling outcomes. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Clinical Supervision Practice
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Introduction to clinical supervision. Includes professional supervision standards, theory, modalities, settings, ethical and legal issues. Course includes supervision of doctoral student supervision experiences. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Professional Leadership and Scholarly Development
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Theories of academic leadership, within professional trends, political and social contexts. Includes developing awareness of scholarly opportunities, including preparation of a professional counseling organization conference proposal. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Pedagogy and the Professorate
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Consideration of pedagogy including teaching, learning, governance, curriculum development, assessment and evaluation. Includes knowledge of accreditation processes, personal and professional challenges of faculty life and exploration of doctoral-level career paths. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Doctoral Comprehensive Exam
courses.desc: Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Students will successfully complete four doctoral Comprehensive Examination Essays read by all members of the student's Doctoral Comps Committee. At least one of the essays is to be submitted for publication. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Qualitative Research I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to graduate students. This course explores and contrasts philosophical assumptions of qualitative and quantitative research. Various methodologies and approaches to qualitative research are reviewed and applications discussed.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Qualitative Research II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to graduate students. This course covers the design, data collection, analysis, and writing of a qualitative research proposal and results. Students practice using qualitative data collection and analysis procedures.

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Methods in Counselor Education and Professional Counseling
courses.desc: (R-18) Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Supervised advanced counselor education methods and approaches that address the professional leadership roles of counselor education, including realms of teaching and advising, clinical supervision, scholarly work and professional counseling practice. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-24) Offered intermittently. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: COUN
courses.title: Thesis/Dissertation
courses.desc: (R-14) Offered intermittently. Prereq., EDLD 620 or EDLD 625. Restricted to students in the Counselor Education and Counselor Education and Supervision programs. Preparation of a dissertation, thesis, professional paper, or manuscript based on research for presentation and/or publication. Credit/No Credit grading only. Level: Graduate

courses.desc: (R-8) Continuation and synthesis of preceding seminars. Level: Graduate

courses.desc: (R-24) Offered summer. Exploration of art forms to develop new artistic and communicative perceptions and awareness. Level: Graduate

courses.desc: (R-4) Offered summer. Creative/research activities. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Montana Writers Live
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn. Open to all majors. An introduction to Montana’s practicing creative writers and their work through reading, live performances and discussion. Regional poets and prose writers will read from their work and lead class discussion. Students prepare questions developed from readings and criticism.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Introductory Fiction Workshop
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Offered on Mountain Campus and at Missoula College. This beginning writing workshop emphasizes the reading, discussion, and revision of students' short fiction. Students will be introduced to the technical elements of writing fiction. No prior experience in writing short fiction required.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Introductory Poetry Workshop
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. This beginning writing workshop focuses on the reading, discussion, and revision of students' poems. Students will study and use models of poetic techniques. No prior experience in writing poetry required.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Introductory Nonfiction Workshop
courses.desc: A study of the art of nonfiction through reading and responding to contemporary nonfiction and the writing of original nonfiction works. Focus is on creative expression, writing technique and nonfiction forms. Students begin with writing exercises and brief essays, advancing to longer forms as the semester progresses.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: The Oval: Literary Magazine
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered Spring, Mountain Campus. This course is open to undergraduates who have completed at least one semester of creative writing. Students focus on the editing, design, layout and marketing of The Oval, University of Montana's undergraduate literary magazine. Students will read, discuss and develop responses to to recongnized literary works, as well as developing criteria for each volume's content and design. The class will include the evaluation and selection of fiction, nonfiction, poetry and visual art submissions to The Oval. Students are required to keep a reading journal, and compile a portfolio of writing exercises, responses to texts and critiques of published works.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Intermediate Fiction Workshop
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., CRWR 210A. An intermediate fiction writing workshop. Students will be expected to finish 3 or 4 substantial stories for the course. Although some outside material will be considered, the primary emphasis will be analysis and discussion of student work.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Intermediate Poetry Workshop
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., CRWR 211A. An intermediate workshop involving critical analysis of students' work-in-progress as well as reading and discussion of poems in an anthology. Numerous directed writing assignments, experiments, exercises focused on technical considerations like diction, rhythm, rhyme, and imagery.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Intermediate Nonfiction Workshop
courses.desc: (R-9) Prereq., CRWR 212A or CRWR 210A. An intermediate nonfiction workshop. Students read and respond to model essays, in addition to creating and revising original essays for workshop review. Assignments and exercises focus on writing craft and research techniques.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: The Art and Craft of Revision
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered spring. Prereq., CRWR 210A. An intermediate writing course focused on revision of prose works-in-progress and study of narrative, plot, and editing at the language level. Materials include craft manuals, contemporary and classic examples, and student manuscripts.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Advanced Fiction Workshop
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., CRWR 310. An advanced writing workshop in which student manuscripts are read and critiqued. Rewriting of work begun in CRWR 310 will be encouraged. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Advanced Poetry Workshop
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., CRWR 311. An advanced writing workshop involving critical analysis of students' work-in-progress as well as reading and discussion of poems by established poets. Discussions will focus on structure and stylistic refinement with emphasis on revision. Different techniques, schools, and poetic voices will be encouraged. Frequent individual conferences. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Advanced Nonfiction Workshop
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., CRWR 312A. An advanced creative writing workshop focused primarily on reading and writing nonfiction; some classes may focus on personal essay, narrative nonfiction or short forms. Students complete two substantial essays. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Storytelling
courses.desc: This course is open to both undergraduate and graduate students, and is not limited to English majors. In-class exercises and out-of-class assignments are designed to help students identify, develop, and demonstrate effective narrative practices in their chosen fields. Students learn to recognize and identify unifying themes, motifs, and ideas in literature and oral stories. Students will read, write, edit and present stories to the class, as well as providing a critique of their peers' work. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Fiction Capstone
courses.desc: Offered autumn or spring. Restricted to students in the Creative Writing BFA program. Prereq., CRWR 410 or CRWR 411 or CRWR 412 with a minimum grade of B. The BFA capstone is the ultimate course for students prior to graduation. This is a hands-on course and a mentorship, though some elements maybe be offered electronically. Level: Undergraduate

courses.desc: (R-6) Offered Intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.title: Independent Study

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Nonfiction Workshop
courses.desc: (R-15) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to students in the Creative writing MFA program. A creative writing workshop focused primarily on personal essay and narrative nonfiction. Attention given to writing and publishing professional magazine essays. Students complete two substantial essays. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Techniques of Nonfiction
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered once every 2 years. Restricted to students in the Creative writing MFA program. Study of form, technique and style in contemporary nonfiction. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Techniques of Modern Fiction
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Restricted to students in the Creative Writing-Fiction MFA program. Intensive reading of contemporary prose writers. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: CRWR
courses.title: Traditional Prosody
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to students in the Creative writing MFA program. Intensive practice and readings in prosodic and other poetic techniques. Level: Graduate

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-24) Offered intermittently. Restricted to students in the Creative writing MFA program. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered every term. Restricted to students in the Creative writing MFA program. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student and special projects in creative writing. Level: Graduate
