courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered every term. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-24) Offered autumn and spring. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Graduate Practicum
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Supervised, practical experience in a professional setting relevant to the student's field of study. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Final Portfolio Research
courses.desc: Offered spring. Investigation into subjects relevant to the development of the students Final Portfolio work. Application of qualitative research techniques, with a research presentation or paper due at the end of the semester. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Game Design and Interactive Media
courses.desc: (R-6) This course explores advanced and emerging concepts in game design and interactive media, focusing on such topics as innovative mechanics, narrative integration, player psychology, AI, and the impact of technology on gameplay. Students will engage in hands-on projects, critical analysis, and collaborative discussions to deepen their understanding of contemporary game design challenges and trends. This course aims to push students to think critically about the complex layers of game design and encourage them to innovate within the field, preparing them for advanced careers in game development, games research, and emerging interactive media.

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Final Portfolio I
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn. Ongoing production and content work relating to thesis projects. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Media Practicum
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered fall and spring. Pursuit of Practical Experience in Media Arts projects both personal and Professional. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-24) Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Professional Practices
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered every term. Work outside of program in an area of professional interest. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MART
courses.title: Final Portfolio II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered spring. Final work on thesis portfolio. Approval by the student’s thesis committee is required for graduation. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MAR
courses.title: Digital Video Production Technology
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Preqeq., major in Media Arts. A project-based class, students learn the use and application of filmmaking equipment, including cameras, lights and sound. Short film projects are produced to apply principles and work in various roles required for the completion of a fiction film.

courses.subject: MAR
courses.title: Screenwriting
courses.desc: Offered spring. This course is devoted to short films, with an emphasison writing camera-ready scripts for production. Feature film structure and techniques are also introduced.

courses.subject: MAR
courses.title: Experimental Film
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Media Arts majors only. Surveying a wide range of experimental cinema (film/video) from the 1920's to the present with the central focus being artistic practice in the context of historic and cultural concerns. Students will also create projects focusing on exploring film/video both as a form of personal expression and as a medium, rather than as mass entertainment. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to Manufacturing Processes
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. This course is designed to introduce the student with an overview of manufacturing to include engineering materials and product attributes, material removal processes, property enhancing and surface processing operations, special processes and assembly technologies, and manufacturing systems.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to Manufacturing Materials
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. This is an introductory course in the study of materials used in the manufacturing industry. Topics include selection and identification of steels, selection and identification of nonferrous metals, mechanical behavior of various plastics, hardening, case hardening, tempering, annealing, normalizing, stress relieving, and the use of the Rockwell and Brinell hardness testers.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Related Metals Processes I
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Use of hand tools and machines which relate to the repair of heavy equipment. Instruction covers fasteners, layout, bench metal, threads and threading, drills and drilling, and tool sharpening.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Related Metals Processes II
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., or corequisite, M 105. Instruction and use of drills, files, threads and threading processes, basic lathe, drill press, and band saw operation, including precision measuring instruments. Fasteners, layout procedures, and basic hand tools are covered.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Related Metals Processes III
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., or corequisite, M 105. A basic metalworking course covering fasteners, layout, bench metal, heat treating, threads and threading, drills and drilling, basic machining, and tool sharpening.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Blueprint Reading & Interpretation for Machining
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. This course introduces the fundamental concepts necessary to interpret and make drawings with symbols, various schematics and diagrams, dimensioning techniques, section views, auxiliary views, threads and fasteners, and sketching typical to all shop drawings. Interpretation of specifications and determination of acceptable tolerance requirements to ensure quality control measures for design parts will also be stressed.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to CAM
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. This course introduces Computer Aided Manufacturing (CAM) operational basics for both mill and lathe programming using current CAM software. The course includes terminology relevant to PC-based CAD/CAM work, hardware familiarity, system operation and management, folders, file type and structure, menu structure and use, and 3 axis (milling machines) and 2 axis (lathes) tool paths. Emphasis is placed on proper geometric creation, management, relevant utilities, and toolbar and menu functions.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to CNC Lathes
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., MCH 132. This course provides opportunities for students to develop skills in the safe setup, maintenance, and operation of CNC lathes and related periphery tools and skills. Topics covered include CNC lathe parts, controls, tool holding, tool insert geometry, chip formation, speeds and feeds, operation and process planning, threads, fits, dimensioning and tolerances, surface finish, and the following lathe processes: facing, turning, tapering, drilling, boring, reaming, chamfering, grooving, parting-off, internal and external threading, tapering, and knurling. Graded projects based on chuck, collet, and fixturing will be done. Related periphery tooling, use and care of precision measuring tools, in addition to related math used in the trade, will also be covered.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to CNC Mills
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq., MCH 134. This course provides instruction in the setup and operation of CNC mills. Student projects include specialty tooling and multi-axis machining. Students will also gain experience in process control. Topics include specialty tooling, multi-axis machining, process control, and laboratory exercises in part production.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Machine Quality Control and Precision Measurements
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Students will develop the knowledge to analyze and evaluate the processes and methodology required in an industrial production environment to determine whether quality control standards are being met. Topics include use of non-precision measuring tools, use of precision measuring tools, use of comparison gauges, and analysis of measurements in a CNC environment.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Machine Shop
courses.desc: Offered spring. Offered at Missoula College. The course content covers a broad range of shop fundamentals in manual and CNC machining. This course includes an emphasis on shop and work area safety. Instruction covers standard shop work, such as measurement, layout, basic hand tools, drills, drill presses, and taps and dies. Use of pedestal grinder will be covered. Work assignments incorporate projects requiring use of the above machines, tooling, and emphasizes safety.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to Manual Engine Lathes
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq./corereq., MCH 120 and MCH 129. This introduction to Manual Engine Lathes will cover the safety, maintenance and operation of manual engine lathes and related periphery tools and skills. Subjects covered include HSS tool bit grinding and tool bit geometry, chip formation, speeds and feeds, operation and process planning, threads, fits, dimensioning and tolerances, surface finish, and the following lathe processes: facing, turning, tapering, drilling, boring, reaming, chamfering, grooving, parting-off, internal and external threading, tapering, knurling, filing and polishing. Graded projects using between centers and chuck work turning will be done. Related periphery tooling, use and care of precision measuring tools, in addition to related math used in the trade, will also be covered.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Introduction to Manual Mills
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Offered at Missoula College. Prereq./co-req., MCH 120 and MCH 129. The student will perform advanced hands-on machine shop operations: set up and operation of manual milling machines, drill presses, band saws, grinders, and other equipment commonly found in manufacturing facilities. The student will use precision measuring tools and methods, utilize blueprints, and perform project process planning. Various types of steel and aluminum are use.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6). Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Manufacturing Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Guided study in a specialized workforce education area.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Manufacturing Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Offered at Missoula College. Guided study in a specialized workforce education area.

courses.subject: MCH
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered at Missoula College. Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Introduction to the Army
courses.desc: Offered autumn. The Constitutional role of the military, military tradition, current defense posture, service roles and missions. An introduction to issues and competencies that are central to a commissioned officer’s responsibilities. Establishes framework for understanding officership, leadership and army values.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Intro to Tactical Leadership
courses.desc: Offered spring. Establishes foundation of basic leadership fundamentals such as problem–solving, communications, goal setting and improving listening techniques. Introduction to the principles of military leadership and organizational values through discussion, observation and practice exercises.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Army Physical Fitness
courses.desc: (R-10) Offered autumn and spring. The study and application of military drill and ceremony: formation, ceremonies, and marching; the study of the fundamentals of the military physical conditioning program, and the practical application of skills learned. Physical education activity course; a maximum of four credits of activity courses may be counted toward graduation.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Innovative Team Leadership
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Demonstration and practice of individual military leadership skills with emphasis on communication and observation through experiential learning exercises. Establishes framework for understanding of “life skills” such as physical fitness and time management. Examination and practical application of tasks training and military style briefings.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Found of Tactical Leadership
courses.desc: Offered spring. Building successful teams through influencing actions and effective communication in setting and achieving goals. Use of creativity in the problem solving process. Introduction of individual and team aspects of military tactics in small unit operations. Practical exercises in techniques for training others as an aspect of continued leadership development.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Ranger Challenge
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn. Students must be physically qualified and enrolled in an additional MSL academic class. Practical hands–on training in one rope bridge, land navigation, military weapons assembly/disassembly and physical conditioning. A team selected from this class will represent the University in competition against four other colleges and universities within the Big Sky Task Force. Physical education activity course; a maximum of four credits of activity courses may be counted toward graduation.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: American Military History
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Describes the evolution of the American military land forces within the context of national historical development, industrialization, national security, and the United States' evolving international role and policies.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one–time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Training Management and Warfighting Fundamentals
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Developing personal leadership principles through the learning and application of various small unit leadership procedures. Fundamentals of leadership development, land navigation, troop leading, small units tactics, rappelling, rifle marksmanship and physical fitness. Study of the organization and operation of the U.S. Army as a profession. Students are required to attend one weekend field exercise during the semester. Restricted to contracted Military Science students.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Applied Team Leadership
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to contracted Military Science students. Continuation of the study and application of small unit leadership tasks. Advanced leadership skills taught including medical evacuation procedures, radio procedures, and increased involvement in planning and executing military operations in preparation for attendance at the Leader Development and Assessment Course at Fort Lewis, Washington. Students participate in rifle marksmanship instruction including qualification with the M16A2 rifle, rappelling, and attend one weekend exercise with students from regional universities in the area and the Montana Army National Guard.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership Laboratory
courses.desc: (R-10) Offered autumn and spring. Practical application of skills learned in the classroom.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership Development and Assessment Course
courses.desc: Offered every term. Required study and internship in military tactics, leadership and organizational behavior. Supervised by active duty military officers. Participants attend course of study at Fort Knox, KY for four weeks of intense evaluation and training to assess their ability to serve as a 2nd LT in the US Army, US Army Reserves, or the National Guard.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R–9) Offered autumn and spring. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one–time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: The Army Officer
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to contracted Military Science students. The application of leadership principles and techniques involved in leading young men and women in today’s Army. Students explore training management. methods of effective staff collaboration and developmental counseling techniques. Develops student proficiency in planning and executing complex operations, functioning as a member of a staff and mentoring subordinates. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership in a Complex World
courses.desc: Offered spring. Restricted to contracted Military Science students. Study includes case study of military law and practical exercises on establishing an ethical command climate. Examines the role communications, values and ethics play in effective leadership. Students complete a semester long Senior Leadership Project that requires them to plan, organize, collaborate, analyze and demonstrate their leadership skills. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Coop. Education/Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered every term. Required study and internship in military tactics, leadership and organizational behavior. Supervised by active duty military officers. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Enjoyment of Music
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. The development of music listening skills. Exploration of the relationship between musical materials and the expressive qualities of a musical composition or performance. Concert attendance required. No musical background is expected.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Performance Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Individual instruction in voice, piano, organ, harpsichord, carillon, string, wind and percussion instruments. All private instruction requires concurrent ensemble participation. A maximum of 6 credits is allowed in music performance.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Fundamentals
courses.desc: Offered intermittenly. Basic principles of notation, including clefs, scales, intervals, chords and rhythm.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Coreq., MUSI 140. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and Theatre majors in the Musical Theater Performance concentration. Material and structure of music. Application of principles in two-, three-, and four-part writing and the keyboard.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSI 105. Coreq., MUSI 141. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and Theatre majors in the Musical Theater Performance concentration. Continuation of MUSI 105.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Orchestra: UMSO
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Rehearsal and performing experience in a broad range of symphonic, choral, operatic and concerto repertoire in the University Orchestra and the Missoula Symphony. Participation in the Missoula Symphony also requires an audition.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Opera Theatre I
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Study and performance of the standard opera repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Group Voice Class
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. This course introduces skills that enable and enhance healthy singing, including proper vocal technique, performance skills, and artistic presentation. It is taught in a group setting and is appropriate to all skill levels. Students do not have to read music in order to succeed in this course.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Choir
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Different sections of this course comprise the lower-division sections of the University Choir (Section 01) and Chamber Chorale (Section 02). University Choir requires a voice placement to be completed prior to the first rehearsal. The voice placement is an assessment of the student’s voice and capabilities in order to place them in the correct section within the choir. Participation in Chamber Chorale is contingent upon successful completion of a two-part audition process that includes an audition and a callback, which must also be completed prior to the first rehearsal. Students may visit https://www.umt.edu/music/academics/ensembles/vocal-ensembles/choirs/default.php for more information and to complete the Voice Placement Registration Form.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Band: UM Concert Band
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Major musical organizations open to all University students. Audition required for Symphonic Wind Ensemble.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Percussion Ensemble: UM
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Ensemble for percussionists.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: World Percussion Ensemble
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Ensemble for percussionists exploring global musical styles.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: History of Jazz
courses.desc: Offered autumn. The development of jazz in the 20th century with emphasis on critical listening and the recognition of important trends and people in its history.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Ensemble I: UM Jazz Bands
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Study and performance of the jazz repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: History of Rock & Roll
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. A study of the roots, components, and development of the musical art form "Rock and Roll". Significant performing artists and movements with the style identified and presented. Includes traditional lecture with substantial use of audio and visual aids.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Country Music: Cowboys, Opry, and Nashville
courses.desc: This course will explore the country music genre, including its major performers, songwriters, songs and impact on culture from the early times on the radio to the beginning of the twenty-first century.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Skills I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to majors and minors in Music, majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration, majors in Sound Design and Media Technology, and students seeking the Certificate in Sound Production Fundamentals. Music reading, techniques, and harmonization skills acquired through study of solo and ensemble repertoire in a contemporary electronic piano laboratory.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Skills II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSI 135A. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration. Continuation of MUSI 135A.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Aural Perception I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Coreq., MUSI 105. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration. A laboratory course in singing and dictation to supplement Theory I.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Aural Perception II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSI 140. Coreq., MUSI 106. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration. Continuation of MUSI 140.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Grizzly Marching Band
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn. A musical organization of brass, woodwinds, percussion, and auxiliary units open to all University students with no audition required.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Beginning Guitar
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. A beginning course in the fundamentals of playing folk guitar. Includes introduction to the rudiments of music.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Chamber Ensembles I
courses.desc: (R-20) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. String, woodwind, brass, percussion, piano and vocal ensembles as appropriate to meet student needs.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composition I
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in Sound Design and Media Technology. An introduction to the basic art of music composition. May be substituted for upper-division electives for students not majoring in theory or composition.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Students must have projects approved by a music faculty member before enrolling.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Study I
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration. Instruction in voice, piano, organ, string, wind, and percussion instruments. Students entering MUSI 195 must show talent for solo performance and evidence of prior study. All private instruction for music majors requires concurrent ensemble participation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory III
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., MUSI 106 and MUSI 141. Coreq., MUSI 240. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Continuation of MUSI 106. Topics focus on notational literacy as reflected in, but not limited to, music as defined by and expressed in the Western European historical tradition from the Renaissance through the common practice period to the contemporary musical world in which we live.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory IV
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSI 205. Coreq., MUSI 241. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. This course is a continuation of MUSI 205, concentrating on, but not limited to, music as defined by and expressed in the Western European historical traditions from the Renaissance through the common practice period to the contemporary musical world in which we live.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: World Music (equiv to 307)
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Introduction to the diversity of music among the world's people. Selected music systems throughout the world examined in their broad culture contexts: religious, historical, and social. Introduction to ethnomusicology-a combination of musicology, anthropology and other related disciplines.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Instrumental Piano Classical
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Requires a placement examination. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Accelerated offering of the material covered in MUSI 235 and 236.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Skills III
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., MUSI 136A. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Continuation of MUSI 136A.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Skills IV
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSI 235. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Continuation of MUSI 235. Culminates in piano functional examination.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Aural Perception III
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Prereq., MUSI 106 and MUSI 141. Coreq., MUSI 205. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. A lab course in singing and dictation to supplement Theory III.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Aural Perception IV
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSI 240. Coreq., MUSI 206. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. A lab course in singing and dictation to supplement Theory IV.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composer's Workshop
courses.desc: (R-20) Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. This is a composition workshop and new music ensemble in which student composers and performers collaborate, guided by a faculty composer, to develop new pieces.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composition II
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 180. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Original work in composition may be substituted for upper-division electives for students not majoring in theory or composition.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Diction: English, Italian
courses.desc: Offered autumn even-numbered years. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Introduces students to the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) with application to American English diction and Italian diction.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Diction: German & French (equiv 382)
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. Prereq., MUSI 281. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Applies IPA to French and German diction and addresses other guidelines that apply to the lyric pronunciation of these languages. Students will transcribe, translate, recite, and sing German and French texts. Students who would like to be considered for mid-year registration in this diction series may do so only with the consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings by visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Study II
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 195 and audition. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Instruction in voice, piano, organ, string, wind and percussion instruments. Continuation of 195. All private instruction requires concurrent ensemble participation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Upper-Division Required Performance
courses.desc: Restricted to majors and minors in Music. All music majors must present a juried performance on their primary instrument that demonstrates competency in the musical skills necessary to proceed in their degree track. Graded CR/NCR.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music History I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. The history of music in Western civilization from its origins to 1750 and its relationship to general cultural development. Introduction to basic research skills in music. Emphasis on listening for style characteristics through representative recorded repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music History II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., WRIT 101. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in Sound Design and Media Technology. The history of music in Western civilization from 1750 to modern times.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Sound in the Natural World
courses.desc: Offered even-numbered years. This is a music composition and performance course that explores sound/music in relation to wilderness. Students will learn from cultures that have stayed in contact with their natural environment and will create compositions from materials collected in the field and will perform and critique them. As a result, students will become familiar with their own creative process.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Orchestras II: UM
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 108A. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing in instrument of participation. Rehearsal and performing experience in a broad range of symphonic, choral, operatic, and concerto repertoire in the University Orchestra and the Missoula Symphony.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Opera Theatre II
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 108A. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Study and performance of the standard opera repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Choir III
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to students with upper-division standing in voice. Different sections of this course comprise the upper-division sections of the University Choir (Section 01) and Chamber Chorale (Section 02). University Choir requires a voice placement to be completed prior to the first rehearsal. The voice placement is an assessment of the student’s voice and capabilities in order to place them in the correct section within the choir. Participation in Chamber Chorale is contingent upon successful completion of a two-part audition process that includes an audition and a callback, which must also be completed prior to the first rehearsal. Students may visit https://www.umt.edu/music/academics/ensembles/vocal-ensembles/choirs/default.php for more information and to complete the Voice Placement Registration Form.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Band III: UM Concert Band
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to students with upper-division standing in instrument of participation. Major musical organizations open to all University students. Audition required for Symphonic Wind Ensemble.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: UM Percussion Ensemble
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Ensemble for percussionists.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: World Percussion Ensemble
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Ensemble for percussionists exploring global musical styles.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Ensemble II: UM
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Study and performance of the jazz repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Advanced Functional Piano
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors and minors in music with upper-division standing. Techniques of harmonization, transposition, sight-reading, modulation, and improvisation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Practicum in Piano Pedagogy
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered intermittently. Prereq. or coreq., MUSI 435 or MUSI 436. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Student teaching of young pianists.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Instrumental Conducting
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered spring. Prereq., MUSE 239 and MUSI 296. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Conducting methods and practice. Teaching methods and materials.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Choral Conducting
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn. Prereq., MUSE 239 and MUSI 296. Restricted to majors and minors in music with upper-division standing. Provides students with an introduction to choral conducting, score study, and rehearsal techniques. Students will develop an understanding of physical gesture as it relates to leading choral rehearsals and performances using a variety of literature.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Repertoire I
courses.desc: Offered autumn odd-numbered years. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Comprehensive acquaintance with styles and interpretation in British, German, and possible additional repertoire genres.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Repertoire II
courses.desc: Offered spring even-numbered years. Prereq., MUSI 342. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Comprehensive acquaintance with styles and interpretation in American, French and possible additional genres.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Grizzly Marching Band II
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn. Prereq., MUSI 155A. A musical organization of brass, woodwinds, percussion, and auxiliary units open to all University students.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Form & Analysis
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Detailed harmonic and formal analysis of representative works from the Baroque period to the present.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Theory & Improvisation I (equivalent to 225)
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. A performance oriented course to provide a basic understanding of jazz harmony. Application of scales and melodic patterns in improvising over various harmonic progressions.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Chamber Ensemble III: UM
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music and majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration. String, woodwind, brass, percussion, piano and vocal ensembles as appropriate to meet student needs.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composition III
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 280. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Creative writing of music.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music for Dance
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Requires consent of instructor. Interdisciplinary course bringing together creators of music and dance to develop, explore, and perform new music and movement together in performance. Students analyze historic and contemporary dance music and design and create a collaborative live performance for their final project.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Concert Attendance UM
courses.desc: Restricted to majors and minors in Music. All music majors must attend a minimum of 100 approved recitals/concerts prior to graduation. Students will receive recital credits each semester they are enrolled and should register for 388 the semester they apply for graduation. Successful completion of attendance requirements will be graded CR.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Students must have projects approved by a music faculty member before enrolling.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Study III
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 295 and MUSI 296. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Instruction in voice, piano, organ, string, wind and percussion instruments. All private instruction requires concurrent ensemble participation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Junior Recital
courses.desc: Coreq., MUSI 395. Offered autumn and spring. Public performance guided by applied music faculty during the junior year of applied study. This recital, consisting of a minimum of 20 minutes of music, may be scheduled in conjunction with another student’s junior recital.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Counterpoint I
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with upper-division standing. Writing and analysis of contrapuntal styles through the 18th century. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: String Pedagogy & Literature
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Procedures and materials in class string instruction. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Woodwind Pedagogy
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Procedures and materials in individual and class instruction are discussed. Philosophies, repertoire, individual and group techniques used in teaching woodwinds. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Brass Pedagogy
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Procedures and materials in individual and class instruction are discussed. Philosophies, repertoire, individual and group techniques used in teaching brass instruments. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Percussion Pedagogy
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Procedures and materials in individual and class instruction are discussed. Philosophies, repertoire, individual and group techniques used in teaching percussion instruments. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music 20th Century to Present
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Prereq., WRIT 101 and MUSI 302H. Restricted to majors and minors in Music, majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration, and majors in Sound Design and Media Technology with upper-division standing. Detailed analysis and comparison of selected instrumental, vocal and keyboard compositions of the 20th Century. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Topics in Music History
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Prereq., WRIT 101 and MUSI 302H. Restricted to majors and minors in Music, majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration, and majors in Sound Design and Media Technology with upper-division standing. Course materials will examine the development of musical styles, genres, forms and aesthetics important to Western music, introducing students to research methods in musicology. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Cultural Studies in Music
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Prereq., WRIT 101 and MUSI 302H. Restricted to majors and minors in Music, majors in the Musical Theatre Performance concentration, and majors in Sound Design and Media Technology with upper-division standing. Course materials will examine music's contemporary role within cultures and societies around the world, introducing students to research methods in cultural studies and ethnomusicology. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Music Theory
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered intermittently. Prereq., MUSI 206. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Special topics in advanced music theory and analysis. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Pedagogy
courses.desc: (R-6) Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Course materials explore contemporary approaches to music pedagogy and instruction.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Pedagogy
courses.desc: Offered spring even-numbered years. Restricted to majors in music with upper-division or graduate standing. Development of skills needed to rehearse and direct jazz ensembles at the middle school through high school level. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Literature
courses.desc: Offered autumn even-numbered years. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Keyboard literature from the developments of the Baroque era to the contemporary period including the suite, sonata, character pieces, etc. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Literature II
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Keyboard literature from the developments of the Baroque era to the contemporary period including the suite, sonata, character pieces, etc. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Methods & Materials I
courses.desc: Offered autumn odd-numbered years. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Methods and materials for teaching piano classes in public schools and private studios. Procedures in teaching beginning, intermediate and advanced students in private studios. Practical demonstrations and supervised laboratory experience with children's classes. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Methods & Materials II
courses.desc: Offered spring even-numbered years. Prereq., MUSI 435. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Continuation of MUSI 435. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Orchestration
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Orchestrating and transcribing for orchestra and band instruments. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Studio Pedagogy and Lit
courses.desc: Offered autumn odd-numbered years or spring even-numbered years. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Procedures, philosophies and terminology used in the teaching of singing. Individual and group techniques. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Advanced Vocal Pedagogy
courses.desc: Offered spring intermittently. Prereq., MUSI 442. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. A detailed examination of foundational vocal technique and science topics including respiration, phonation, resonation, and articulation. Offers students the opportunity to explore current topics in the field and how to approach them as a singer or voice teacher. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Theory & Improvisation II
courses.desc: Prereq., MUSI 360. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Continuation of MUSI 360. Level: Undergraduate/Graduate.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composers' Workshop II
courses.desc: (R-8) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 267A. This is a composition workshop and new music ensemble, in which student composers and performers collaborate, guided by a faculty composer, to develop new pieces. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Arranging & Composition
courses.desc: Offered spring odd-numbered years. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division or graduate standing. Composing and arranging for small to medium sized jazz ensembles. Rhythmic rewriting of melodies, re-harmonization techniques, arranging of pre-existing jazz compositions, and original compositions. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composition IV
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 380. Restricted to majors in Music. A continuation of composition with writing in the larger forms. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Students must have projects approved by a music faculty member before enrolling. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Study IV
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered autumn and spring. Prereq., MUSI 395. Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Instruction in voice, piano, organ, string, wind and percussion instruments. Continuation of MUSI 395. All private instruction requires concurrent ensemble participation. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Senior Recital/Capstone Project
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Secondary Performance Area
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered every term. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Requires an audition. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Advanced Conducting
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Prereq., MUSI 335 and MUSI 336. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Class and/or individual study of the art of conducting with emphasis on performance with university performing groups. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Research in Music
courses.desc: Offered autumn and summer. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Research problems: their statement, organization, techniques, tabulation of materials, and concepts necessary for interpretation of data. Development of a research proposal. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Instrumental Literature
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Concentrated study of symphonic literature or instrumental chamber music literature. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Major Performance Area
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered every term. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Requires audition and consent of instructor. Continuation of MUSI 495. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Ensemble
courses.desc: (R-6) Participation in large music ensembles, including choirs, concert band, symphonic winds, orchestra, and jazz. Audition may be required. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Analytical Techniques I
courses.desc: Offered autumn odd-numbered years. Restricted to graduate students in Music. A survey of the theoretical approach of leading composers from the polyphonic period to the present. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Analytical Techniques II
courses.desc: Offered spring even-numbered years. Prereq., MUSI 554. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Continuation of MUSI 554. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Composition
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Continuation of MUSI 480. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-24) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Students must have projects approved by a music faculty member before enrolling. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Restricted to graduate students in Music. Requires prior approval of the faculty supervisor. Extended classroom experience which provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Thesis/Professional Project
courses.desc: (R-10) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Preparation of a thesis, manuscript, or professional project for presentation and/or publication. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Dissertation
courses.desc: (R-12) Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Preparation of a dissertation, manuscript, or professional project for presentation and/or publication. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Introduction to Music Education
courses.desc: Restricted to majors in Music. This course provides an overview of the multifaceted role of a music teacher. Includes observations of local school music teachers.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: String Instruments in Classical Music I
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered autumn. Restricted to majors in Music. Group instruction for beginning students on violin, viola, cello and bass, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: String Instruments in Classical Music II
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered spring. Restricted to majors in Music. Group instruction for beginning students on violin, viola, cello and bass, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Voice
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered autumn. Restricted to majors in Music. This course examines vocal function and issues associated with the physical processes of singing such as alignment, breathing, creating sound, amplifying (resonating) sound. Additionally, students will learn basic information about becoming a voice teacher (or choral director). Students will also learn about singers' diction, voice classification, and the appropriate assigning of solo classical repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Percussion Instruments I
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered autumn. Restricted to majors in Music. Basic instruction in percussion instruments, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Percussion Instruments II
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered spring. Prereq., MUSE 126. Restricted to majors in Music. Continuation of MUSE 126. Basic instruction in percussion instruments, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Beginning Conducting
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered autumn. Restricted to majors and minors in Music with at least sophomore standing. A study of the foundations of conducting a music ensemble. Emphasis on issues encountered in various ensemble settings, both instrumental and choral. This course is designed to provide students with an introduction to the foundations of conducting gesture, aural skills, and score study. Students will develop an understanding of physical gesture as it relates to leading an ensemble in rehearsals and performances using a variety of literature. The course is divided into four units with each unit corresponding to a particular gestural challenge.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Flute & Single Reed
courses.desc: (R-2) Basic instruction in flute and single-reed instruments, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Double Reed
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered autumn. Basic instruction in oboe and bassoon, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Upper Brass
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered autumn. Restricted to majors in Music. Basic instruction in trumpet and horn, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Lower Brass
courses.desc: (R-2) Offered spring. Restricted to majors in Music. Basic instruction in trombone, baritone, and tuba, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Woodwinds – Clarinet and Saxophone
courses.desc: (R-2) Restricted to majors in Music. Basic instruction in clarinet and saxophone, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Techniques: Woodwinds - Double Reed and Flute
courses.desc: (R-2) Restricted to majors in Music. Basic instruction in double reed instruments (e.g., oboe, bassoon) and flute, with emphasis on teaching procedures.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: General Music Methods & Materials I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Development of practical knowledge to effectively instruct and administer general music classes in the public schools, grades K-12.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: General Music Methods & Materials II
courses.desc: Offered spring. Prereq., MUSE 333. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Continuation of MUSE 333.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Methods: K-8 Music
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Restricted to majors in Education. Integration of fundamental skills and basic rudiments of music into the various aspects of teaching music creatively in the elementary school. For non-music majors only.

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Technology and Materials
courses.desc: Offered autumn semesters. Restricted to majors in Music. The course will provide in-depth examination of technology and print resources appropriate for use in music classrooms K-12, all areas and ensembles. Students will work independently and collaboratively to reflect upon, discuss, and practice utilizing technology and print resources for the music classroom (K-12). Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-9) Restricted to majors and minors in Music. Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Students must have projects approved by a music faculty member before enrolling. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Methods
courses.desc: (R-4) Offered Spring. Prereq., MUSE 123. Restricted to majors in Music with upper-division standing. Development of strategies for directing secondary ensembles. Focus on rehearsal techniques and literature selection. Music Education students must take both choral and instrumental sections once. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Psychology of Music
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. Investigation of the perception, processing and cognition of music. Psychological foundations of musical behavior: psychoacoustics, measurement and prediction of musical ability, functional music, music and society, music learning, and effective response to music. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Philosophy of Music
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Restricted to graduate students in Music. An investigation of the meaning of music, the relationship to various societies and social structures and the leading philosophical ideas which relate to music and music instruction. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUSE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-12) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: MUST
courses.title: Digital Audio & Multitracking
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Composition of computer music through recording, editing, and processing sound with digital audio software. Study of the theory and application of digital audio recording, multitracking, and digital signal processing, and electroacoustic music history. Survey of historical and current electronic and computer music composers, pieces, and practices.

courses.subject: MUST
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Students must have projects approved by a music faculty member before enrolling.

courses.subject: MUST
courses.title: Sequencing, Synthesis, and Sampling
courses.desc: Offered spring even numbered years. Composition of electronic music using digital and analog synthesis methods, including software, hardware, modular, keyboard, and other electronic instruments; exploration of sampling as a composition device and its history in music-making practices; sequencing as a formal and compositional tool and the exploration of its inherent challenges and benefits; MIDI, modulation, and other non-standard input sources as a way of interacting, performing, and improvising with electronic music.

courses.subject: MUST
courses.title: Interactivity and Digital Signal Processing
courses.desc: Offered fall even numbered years. Advanced techniques for processing, mixing, designing, and producing audio in both studio and performance settings using digital, analog, software, and hardware tools; exploring the usage of industry-standard tool sets for digital audio manipulation such as compression, EQ, pitch correction, effects, etc.

courses.subject: MUST
courses.title: Designing the Show
courses.desc: Offered spring odd numbered years. Restricted to student with upper-division standing. This is an interdisciplinary, multimedia course that gives students opportunities to apply complex and detailed knowledge in music, media arts, stage production, and event management in order to create large-scale performance experiences for live audiences. Technology is used to develop and implement new ideas in performance practice, culminating in a final performance event that showcases students creative ideas and skills. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.title: Independent Study

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Introduction to Native American Studies
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Survey course to acquaint the student with Native American Studies by a general overview of Indian history, culture, philosophy, religious beliefs and contemporary issues.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Elementary Blackfoot I
courses.desc: Offered autumn. An introduction to the Blackfoot language and culture. Students will learn how to write and read Blackfoot as well as how to conduct simple conversations.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Elementary Blackfoot II
courses.desc: Offered intermittently spring. Continuation of NASX 141.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Event Planning
courses.desc: Offered spring semester. This course is intended for students to learn the skills necessary to put on a large event. The course is intended as a hands-on experiential learning course. The culmination of the course will be putting on the annual Kyi-Yo contest pow-wow, the first large regional pow-wow of the year on the circuit.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-9) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: (R-6) Extended classroom experience that provides practical application of classroom learning during placements off campus. Prior approval must be obtained from the faculty supervisor. A maximum of 6 credits of Internship (198, 298, 398, 498) may count toward graduation.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Indian Culture Expressed Through Language
courses.desc: Offered autumn. This course has been designed to introduce students to a non-Western perspective of the relationship that exists between Indian cultures and their languages. Students will be exposed to various languages of American Indian peoples, and how through Native languages insight can be gained into history, traditions, and cultural life-ways of Indian peoples.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Native American Sports & Games
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Explores Native American sports and games, both traditional and modern. Through classroom learning and actual play, students gain an understanding of how play and competition have been vital to Native communities.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Indigenous World View Perspectives
courses.desc: Offered spring. Examination of Indigenous belief systems, with regard to world views, religious ceremonies, cultural ways and the impact that Anglo-European culture has had upon these systems. Focus on Indigenous peoples of Australia, New Zealand, Canada and the United States

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Oral and Written Traditions of Native Americans
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. Analysis of the oral traditions of Native Americans including an introduction to the literary works of early leading American Indian writers.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Indigenous Community Development
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. This course introduces the student to concepts in indigenous/rural sustainable community development in the countries of North America in broad historical and cultural frameworks.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Native American Studies Research Theories and Methods
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Prereq., WRIT 101. Introduction to the Research materials pertaining to the study of American Indian peoples and cultures. Emphasis on current research trends and writing.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Ecological Perspectives in Native American Traditions
courses.desc: An examination of Native American environmental ethics and tribal and historical and contemporary use of physical environmental resources.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Native American Beliefs and Philosophy
courses.desc: Offered autumn and spring. A study of selected ethical systems; origins, world views; religious beliefs and the way they have been affected by Western civilization.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Native American Literature
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Selected readings from Native American Literature and criticism with emphasis on the literatures after the Native American literary Renaissance. A minimum of three genres covered and three culture areas.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge
courses.desc: Offered summer. This course is one unit of the four unit Wild Rockies Summer Semester program and explores the traditional ecological perspectives of the Salish, Kootenai, Blackfeet and Tlingit people, as well as how these perspectives relate to Western concepts of ecology. Through field-based activities, lectures by tribal elders, and personal exploration, students will come to a heightened understanding of the still vital cultural perspectives and practices of modern American Indians, particularly in the Rockies of Montana and Canada.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Montana's Indians and Land
courses.desc: Offered autumn. This course is one unit of the four unit Montana Afoot & Afloat: Human/Land Relations fall semester program. This course gives students a greater understanding of Indian people’s traditional relationships with the land in Montana and an understanding of how and why those relationships may have changed. Extensive time will be spent on the Fort Belknap, Northern Cheyenne, and Crow Reservations where the class will meet with tribal elders and learning will have an emphasis on environmental and tribal/land relationships.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Indians of Montana since the Reservation Era
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Examination of the history of Montana Indians since the establishment of the reservations, contemporary conditions, and issues among both reservation and non-reservation Indian communities in the state. Special attention given to social and economic conditions, treaty rights, tribal sovereignty, and legal issues.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Native Americans and Cinema
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Surveys the image of Native Americans in American film with an emphasis on "revisionist," or "breakthrough" films. Ultimate focus will be on films featuring Native American writers, directors and actors.

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Gender Issues in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. Focus on American Indian gender relations and their cultural continuity and historical evolution. National in scope with concentration on certain tribes. Group analysis of contemporary gender issues relevant to Native American peoples. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: American Indian Education
courses.desc: Offered intermittently. An overview of American Indian education including a look at the unique needs of Indian children. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Tribal Sovereignty
courses.desc: Offered spring. An examination of the evolution of tribal governments from a historical and political perspective. Particular attention is devoted to the issues of tribal sovereignty and tribal-state conflicts. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Tribal Governance and Policymaking
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered spring. Prereq., NASX 475. This course examines the evolution of tribal governing structures with a focus on contemporary formal tribal policy making processes, practices, and outcomes. The class concludes with an exploration of the limitations and challenges, as well as the benefits and opportunities, presented to tribal leaders and community members by these modern-day forms of tribal government. Course co-convenes with NASX 579. Level: Undergraduate

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one-time offerings of current topics. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. A review and discussion of current research. Topics vary. Reading Seminar in Native American Studies -- Offered spring. Restricted to majors or minors in Native American Studies with at least junior standing. Senior reading capstone course for the review of past and current literature on and by American Indians. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Practicum
courses.desc: (R-6) Supervised, practical experience in a professional setting relevant to the student's field of study. Level: Undergraduate-Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Senior Capstone/Thesis
courses.desc: (R-9) Restricted to majors or minors in Native American Studies with at least junior standing. Independent research project in Native American Studies supervised by a faculty member and leading to completion of the baccalaureate degree. Level: Undergraduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Indigenous Worldview and Education
courses.desc: The seminar will provide an opportunity for students from multiple sites to engage in the comparative study of issues associated with the education of Indigenous peoples and communities on an international scale with an emphasis on the role of language and culture through a review of educational practices and theories that have emerged from a variety of sources. Students may take the course once or a second year in sequence; some site instructors may change. The course is teleconferenced among University of Montana and the Universities of Hawaii Hilo, Alaska Fairbanks and Anchorage, Arizona, British Columbia, Dene (Navajo) College, and Te Whare Wananga o Awanuiarangi-Whakatane (New Zealand). No prerequisites apply; letter grades given, based on collaborative local and international projects, short response papers, and a term paper. Students be confident in using the internet. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Tribal Governance and Policymaking
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered spring. This course examines the evolution of tribal governing structures with a focus on contemporary formal tribal policy making processes, practices, and outcomes. The class concludes with an exploration of the limitations and challenges, as well as the benefits and opportunities, presented to tribal leaders and community members by these modern-day forms of tribal government. Course co-convenes with NASX 479. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: NASX
courses.title: Native American Studies Research Theories/Methods
courses.desc: Offered autumn. An exploration of research materials pertaining to the study of American Indian peoples and cultures, with an emphasis on current research trends and writing. Level: Graduate

courses.subject: NRSM
courses.title: First Year Seminar in Environmental Science and Sustainability
courses.desc: Offered autumn. This First Year Seminar introduces students to key issues in environmental science and sustainability, with a focus on how science can be applied to problem-solving. Students will also learn about key resources at the university and focus on the skills needed to ensure their success at UM.

courses.subject: NRSM
courses.title: First Year Seminar in Field Studies in Conservation
courses.desc: Offered autumn. Restricted to student with freshman and sophomore standing. Field study focusing on flora and fauna, history of land use and ecological change, contemporary forest management, conservation and community development in western Montana.

courses.subject: NRSM
courses.title: Environmental Science and Sustainability
courses.desc: Offered autumn. An exploration of the major environmental science and sustainability issues facing humankind and the social processes required to manage environmental conflicts. Provides an introduction to the function of ecological systems and the impacts of human uses on the environment and explores strategies for addressing global climate change, ex-urban population growth, and environmental degradation.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.desc: (R-6) Offered intermittently. Experimental offerings of visiting professors, experimental offerings of new courses, or one time offerings of current topics.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.desc: (R-6) Course material appropriate to the needs and objectives of the individual student.
